overall.assessment: Prema dostavljenoj strukturi — bez punog prijepisa iz kojeg bi se mogla provjeriti formulacija pojedinih tvrdnji — podcast djeluje uglavnom usklađeno s kršćanskom antropologijom: osobu ne svodi na njezin grijeh, neuspjeh ili tjelesnu ozljedu, nego je prikazuje kao dijete Božje pozvano na obraćenje, ljubav i služenje. Središnje teme povratka vjeri, bračne vjernosti, prihvaćanja djeteta, oprosta, svjedočenja i đakonskog služenja promiču nadu i kulturu susreta, osobito ondje gdje osobna ranjivost postaje povod za solidarnost, a ne za osudu. Važna je i slika poziva kao odgovora „Bože, evo me“, pod uvjetom da se osobno iskustvo i dojmljivi događaji prikazuju kao poticaj na razlučivanje, a ne kao samodostatan dokaz Božje volje. Glavni oprez odnosi se na mogućnost da se tragedija, invaliditet ili čudesno protumačeni događaji prikažu previše jednostavno kao izravno Božje sredstvo ili potvrda poziva; prema samoj strukturi nije moguće utvrditi događa li se takvo pojednostavljenje u razgovoru.
seeds_of_logos: Polazište „najprije dijete Božje“ potvrđuje dostojanstvo osobe koje ne ovisi o njezinu životnom uspjehu, moralnoj prošlosti, zdravlju ni društvenom položaju.

Prikaz obraćenja iz života obilježenog prazninom prema vjeri može svjedočiti da kršćansko obraćenje uključuje i unutarnju promjenu i promjenu načina života, a ne tek snažan osjećaj ili jednu pobožnu epizodu.

Tema Sandrina poniznog priznanja i obnove ljubavi otvara prostor za istinu, odgovornost i pomirenje u braku; katolička vizija braka istodobno drži zajedno vjernost, strpljivost, milosrđe i ozbiljnost rana koje mogu nastati zbog izdaje.

Sandrina spremnost da prihvati dijete i njezina vjera daju vidljiv prostor zaštiti ljudskog života i obiteljskoj solidarnosti. Crkveno učenje o obitelji traži da se njezine stvarne poteškoće prate milosrdno, bez uljepšavanja patnje i bez isključivanja onih koji je nose.
Molitva koja vodi od agresije prema omekšanju srca, ako je prikazana bez romantiziranja nasilja, može svjedočiti kršćanskom oprostu i mogućnosti obraćenja te graditi kulturu susreta umjesto odmazde.

Knjiga, javno svjedočenje i pastoralna služba predstavljaju vjeru kao dar koji se dijeli i stavlja u službu drugih, a ne kao privatno postignuće. To je u skladu s kršćanskim pozivom da obitelj i vjernici ljubav koju primaju prenose bližnjima.

Prikaz čovjeka s protezom koji biciklom putuje u Međugorje može osporiti poistovjećivanje osobe s njezinim tjelesnim ograničenjem i istaknuti njezinu djelatnost i ustrajnost; važno je pritom da se invaliditet ne pretvori u pritisak da se patnja uvijek mora pretvoriti u herojski uspjeh.
Tematski blok o tome što đakon smije i ne smije može pomoći gledateljima da razlikuju osobno svjedočenje od zaređene službe te da poštuju sakramentalni i crkveni poredak, ako su objašnjenja precizna.
concerns: Naslovni niz tragedija, nesreća, neobičnih podudarnosti, ispita i iskustava na hodočašću mogao bi, ako ih razgovor predstavlja kao nedvojbene potvrde Božje volje, potaknuti pojednostavljeno razlučivanje poziva. Osobno iskustvo može biti važno, ali valja ga provjeravati u molitvi, savjesti, crkvenoj zajednici i odgovarajućoj formaciji.

Povezivanje nesreće s novim početkom treba čuvati od dojma da je Bog uzrokovao ili želio nesreću radi kasnijeg duhovnog dobra. Kršćanska nada može prepoznati mogućnost smisla i služenja usred patnje, a da patnju ne opravdava niti ozlijeđenu osobu obvezuje na javno svjedočenje.

Teme bračne izdaje, oprosta i obnove veze zahtijevaju razlikovanje oprosta od poricanja povrede, automatske obnove povjerenja ili pritiska da se ostane u opasnoj situaciji. Struktura upućuje na bolnu i složenu bračnu povijest, ali bez prijepisa nije moguće procijeniti jesu li takve razlike u podcastu izrečene.

Iz naslova o đakonskom pozivu i ovlastima nije moguće provjeriti jesu li točno predstavljeni služba, granice ovlasti i postupak formacije. Svjedočanstvo o pozivu može biti nadahnjujuće, ali ne bi smjelo zamijeniti crkveno razlučivanje ni stvarati dojam da pojedinačni znakovi sami po sebi jamče poziv na ređenje.
overall.theological_context: Katolički okvir za ove teme povezuje obraćenje i milosrđe s istinom o grijehu i stvarnom pozivu na promjenu života; Katekizam, kako je naveden u crkvenom tekstu, opisuje obraćenje kao trajni put Crkve i odgovor na Božju milosrdnu ljubav. Brak se pritom razumije kao vjerni i strpljivi dar, a nerazrješivost kao dar, ne kao puko nametnuto breme; pastoralno milosrđe mora pratiti konkretne obiteljske rane bez napuštanja istine o bračnoj vjernosti. U duhu *Gaudium et spes* 48, kako ga navodi teološki izvor, kršćanska obitelj svjedoči Božju prisutnost, dok evanđeoska milosrdnost traži da se čovjeku pristupi s ljubavlju, pažnjom i brigom za njegovo dostojanstvo.

overall.assessment_en: According to the provided outline — without a full transcript from which the formulation of individual claims could be verified — the podcast appears mostly aligned with Christian anthropology: it does not reduce the person to their sin, failure, or bodily injury, but presents them as a child of God called to conversion, love, and service. The central themes of returning to faith, marital fidelity, welcoming a child, forgiveness, witnessing, and diaconal service promote hope and a culture of encounter, especially where personal vulnerability becomes an occasion for solidarity rather than condemnation. The image of vocation as the response “God, here I am” is also important, provided that personal experience and striking events are presented as an incentive for discernment, rather than as self-sufficient proof of God's will. The main caution relates to the possibility that tragedy, disability, or miraculously interpreted events might be presented too simply as a direct instrument of God or a confirmation of a vocation; according to the outline alone, it is not possible to determine whether such simplification occurs in the conversation.
overall.theological_context_en: The Catholic framework for these themes connects conversion and mercy with the truth about sin and a real call to a change of life; the Catechism, as cited in the ecclesiastical text, describes conversion as an ongoing path of the Church and a response to God's merciful love. Marriage is thereby understood as a faithful and patient gift, and indissolubility as a gift, not merely an imposed burden; pastoral mercy must accompany concrete family wounds without abandoning the truth of marital fidelity. In the spirit of *Gaudium et spes* 48, as cited by the theological source, the Christian family bears witness to God's presence, while evangelical mercifulness requires that a person be approached with love, attentiveness, and care for their dignity.
seeds_of_logos_en: The starting point “first a child of God” affirms the dignity of the person, which does not depend on their success in life, moral past, health, or social standing.

The depiction of conversion from a life marked by emptiness toward faith can witness that Christian conversion includes both an inner change and a change of lifestyle, rather than just a strong feeling or a single pious episode.

The theme of Sandra's humble confession and the renewal of love opens space for truth, responsibility, and reconciliation in marriage; the Catholic vision of marriage simultaneously holds together fidelity, patience, mercy, and the seriousness of wounds that can arise from betrayal.

Sandra's readiness to accept the child and her faith give visible space to the protection of human life and family solidarity. The Church's teaching on the family demands that its real difficulties be accompanied mercifully, without romanticizing suffering and without excluding those who bear it.

Prayer leading from aggression toward a softening of the heart, if presented without romanticizing violence, can bear witness to Christian forgiveness and the possibility of conversion, and build a culture of encounter instead of retaliation.

The book, public witnessing, and pastoral ministry present faith as a gift that is shared and placed at the service of others, rather than as a private achievement. This is in accordance with the Christian calling that the family and believers pass on the love they receive to their neighbors.

The depiction of a man with a prosthesis traveling by bicycle to Međugorje can challenge equating a person with their physical limitation and highlight their agency and perseverance; it is important, however, that disability does not turn into pressure that suffering must always be turned into heroic success.

The thematic segment on what a deacon may and may not do can help viewers distinguish personal witnessing from ordained ministry and respect the sacramental and ecclesial order, provided that the explanations are precise.
concerns_en: The headline sequence of tragedies, accidents, unusual coincidences, tests, and pilgrimage experiences could, if the conversation presents them as unambiguous confirmations of God's will, encourage a simplified discernment of vocation. Personal experience can be important, but it must be tested in prayer, conscience, the ecclesial community, and proper formation.

Connecting an accident with a new beginning should be guarded against the impression that God caused or willed the accident for the sake of a subsequent spiritual good. Christian hope can recognize the possibility of meaning and service in the midst of suffering, without justifying the suffering or obliging the injured person to public witnessing.

The themes of marital betrayal, forgiveness, and renewal of the relationship require distinguishing forgiveness from denial of injury, automatic renewal of trust, or pressure to remain in a dangerous situation. The outline points to a painful and complex marital history, but without a transcript it is not possible to assess whether such distinctions are articulated in the podcast.

From the titles regarding the diaconal vocation and faculties, it is not possible to verify whether the ministry, boundaries of authority, and formation process are accurately presented. A testimony about a vocation can be inspiring, but it should not replace ecclesial discernment or create the impression that individual signs in themselves guarantee a call to ordination.

sections.subtitle: Zaleđeni mostić i pitanje koje je promijenilo sve: „Bože, zašto?“
sections.screenshot_description: Zlatko Krznarić opisuje trenutak kad se, dužan i bez zdravlja, u bolnici pita „Bože, pa zašto?“
sections.content:
Epizoda podcasta Redefinicija počinje isječkom koji odmah pokazuje težinu priče. **Zlatko Krznarić** prepričava trenutak koji mu je preokrenuo život. Na jednom se zaleđenom mostiću njegov automobil zavrtio. Kad se zaustavio, isprva mu se ništa nije dogodilo. Tada je u njega udarila jedna gospođa i priklještila mu obje noge.

Ishod je bio težak. Desnu su mu nogu liječnici uspjeli „pokrpati“, a lijevu su morali amputirati. Krznarić opisuje kako se preko noći našao u bolnici *„dužan, slomljen, opljačkan, bez zdravlja“*. Postavio je pitanje koje si postavlja svatko pogođen tragedijom: **„Bože, pa zašto?“**

Tim isječkom voditelj uvodi slušatelje u razgovor o padu, predanju i novom početku. Naslov epizode to sažima ovako: fatalna nesreća bila je gostov novi početak.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak opisuje tešku nesreću i pitanje „Bože, zašto?“ bez tvrdnje da je patnja Božja kazna ili da Bog izravno uzrokuje nesreću, pa je prikaz u skladu s katoličkim razumijevanjem ljudske patnje kao stvarnog otajstva. Budući da se odlomak prekida prije odgovora na to pitanje, nije moguće procijeniti kako podcast teološki tumači nesreću.
concerns: Nedovršeni odlomak ne pokazuje hoće li se pitanje „zašto?“ povezati s povjerenjem u Boga i Kristovom blizinom patnicima ili s neutemeljenim zaključcima o Božjoj krivnji, kazni ili namjeri.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička vjera ne zabranjuje vapaj ni pitanja u patnji: i biblijski likovi i Isus na križu iznose bol pred Boga, dok Crkva priznaje da na pitanje o patnji nema lakih odgovora. Kršćanski pogled ne tvrdi da Bog uklanja svaku patnju, nego da je u Kristu ulazi u ljudsku patnju i može iz zla izvesti dobro, iako način toga često ostaje otajstvo.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage describes a severe accident and the question "God, why?" without claiming that suffering is God's punishment or that God directly causes the accident, so the presentation is in accordance with the Catholic understanding of human suffering as a real mystery. Since the passage breaks off before the answer to that question, it is not possible to assess how the podcast theologically interprets the accident.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic faith does not forbid crying out nor questions in suffering: both biblical figures and Jesus on the cross bring pain before God, while the Church acknowledges that there are no easy answers to the question of suffering. The Christian view does not claim that God removes all suffering, but that in Christ He enters into human suffering and can bring good out of evil, although the manner of this often remains a mystery.
concerns_en: The unfinished passage does not show whether the question "why?" will be connected with trust in God and Christ's closeness to those who suffer, or with unfounded conclusions about God's guilt, punishment, or intention.

sections.subtitle_en: A frozen little bridge and the question that changed everything: "God, why?"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Zlatko Krznarić describes the moment when, in debt and without health, in the hospital he asks, "God, why?"
sections.content_en:
The episode of the podcast Redefinicija begins with a clip that immediately shows the gravity of the story. **Zlatko Krznarić** recounts the moment that turned his life around. On a frozen little bridge, his car spun out. When it stopped, at first nothing happened to him. Then a lady crashed into him and pinned both of his legs.

The outcome was severe. Doctors managed to "patch up" his right leg, and they had to amputate the left one. Krznarić describes how overnight he found himself in the hospital *"in debt, broken, robbed, without health"*. He asked the question that anyone struck by tragedy asks themselves: **"God, why?"**

With this clip, the host introduces the listeners to a conversation about falling, surrender, and a new beginning. The title of the episode summarizes it like this: the fatal accident was the guest's new beginning.

sections.subtitle: Tko je Zlatko Krznarić? „Najprije dijete Božje“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost odgovara na voditeljevo pitanje „Tko je Zlatko Krznarić?“
sections.content:
Voditelj pozdravlja gosta riječima „Hvaljen Isus i Marija i sveti Josip!“ i predstavlja ga kao brata u Kristu. Zlatko Krznarić je katolički suprug, otac petero djece i vozač po zanimanju. Trenutno studira kako bi, ako Bog da, jednoga dana postao đakon. Prije razgovora o tom, kako ga sam gost naziva, „jako turbulentnom“ razdoblju, voditelj postavlja „filozofsko pitanje“: tko je zapravo Zlatko Krznarić?

Gost odgovara bez oklijevanja: *„Najprije dijete Božje. Na to sam ponosan.“* Zatim nabraja svoje uloge:

- otac,
- suprug,
- brat,
- i prije svega netko tko „želi ljubiti Gospodina“.

Sa suprugom **Sandrom**, koju naziva „najboljom ženom na svijetu“, oženjen je već 27 godina. Njihov obiteljski život opisuje kao „pun uspona i padova“, ali i pun vjernosti i ljubavi koja ih kroz sve to „diže uvijek“.

magisterium.assessment: Izjava „najprije dijete Božje” u skladu je s katoličkim naukom: krštenjem ljudi postaju posinjena djeca Božja u Kristu, što je temeljni kršćanski identitet. Navedene obiteljske i profesionalne uloge te želja za trajnim đakonatom ne proturječe tom identitetu; iz dostupnog odlomka ne proizlazi teološki problem.
magisterium.enrichment: Biti dijete Božje nije tek slikovit naziv, nego dar posinjenja po krštenju i poziv na život u Kristu. Trajni đakonat jest služenje liturgiji, naviještanju Riječi i ljubavi, a za oženjenog kandidata razlučivanje treba uključivati obitelj i suglasnost supruge te čuvati sklad bračnih i crkvenih obveza.

magisterium.assessment_en: The statement "first of all a child of God" is in accordance with Catholic teaching: through baptism, people become adopted children of God in Christ, which is the foundational Christian identity. The mentioned family and professional roles and the desire for the permanent diaconate do not contradict that identity; no theological problem arises from the available excerpt.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Being a child of God is not merely a figurative term, but a gift of adoption through baptism and a call to life in Christ. The permanent diaconate is a service to the liturgy, the proclamation of the Word, and charity, and for a married candidate, discernment should include the family and the wife's consent, and preserve the harmony of marital and ecclesial obligations.

sections.subtitle_en: Who is Zlatko Krznarić? "First of all a child of God"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest answers the host's question "Who is Zlatko Krznarić?"
sections.content_en:
The host greets the guest with the words "Praised be Jesus and Mary and Saint Joseph!" and introduces him as a brother in Christ. Zlatko Krznarić is a Catholic husband, father of five children, and a driver by profession. He is currently studying so that, God willing, one day he might become a deacon. Before the conversation about that, as the guest himself calls it, "very turbulent" period, the host asks a "philosophical question": who actually is Zlatko Krznarić?

The guest answers without hesitation: *"First of all a child of God. I am proud of that."* Then he lists his roles:

- father,
- husband,
- brother,
- and above all someone who "wants to love the Lord".

He has been married to his wife **Sandra**, whom he calls "the best woman in the world", for 27 years already. He describes their family life as "full of ups and downs", but also full of fidelity and love that "always lifts" them through all of it.

sections.subtitle: Život bez Boga: tulumi, motor i sve dublja praznina
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje osjećaj samoće i praznine u razdoblju bez Boga
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da se život svakog obraćenika dijeli na dva dijela, prije i poslije susreta s Kristom, te pita kako je izgledao gostov život prije obraćenja.

Krznarić to naziva „klasikom“. Primio je sve sakramente na vrijeme, a onda je došao pubertet i vjera mu je postala „tlaka“. Godine 1993., s 21 godinom, **odbacio je Boga**. Počeo je razmišljati i živjeti svjetovno: tulumario je, aktivno se bavio sportom, imao vlastiti novac, auto i motor. Izvana je sve to, kaže, „lijepo izgledalo“.

Ta je faza trajala svega nekoliko mjeseci, otprilike pola godine. Uz svjetovni užitak sve je jače osjećao **samoću i prazninu**. Priznaje da je njegova vjera i ranije bila više „reda radi“, iz tradicije i odgoja, bez pravog žara. Ipak, ta mu je vjera očito značila mnogo, jer mu je bez nje „nešto falilo“.

Prekretnica je bila **velika ispovijed kod fra Ante Barišića** koja je trajala sat vremena. Kad je dobio odrješenje, s njega je, kako opisuje, „pao ogromno blato“ i izašao je „kao novi čovjek“. Od toga trenutka, kaže, nastoji živjeti „punim plućima za Gospodina“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak prikazuje osobno svjedočanstvo o udaljavanju od Boga i ne tvrdi da je sama svjetovna razonoda ili posjedovanje stvari nužno grijeh. Njegov je prikaz uglavnom spojiv s kršćanskim govorom o obraćenju, ali tvrdnja da se život „svakog obraćenika” dijeli na razdoblje prije i poslije susreta s Kristom može previše pojednostaviti različite putove obraćenja.
concerns: Izraz da se život svakog obraćenika dijeli na dva dijela može sugerirati jednako nagao ili dramatičan obrazac za sve; crkveno učenje poznaje temeljne prekretnice, ali i postupno te svakodnevno obraćenje.
Opis tulumarenja, sporta, novca, automobila i motora sam po sebi ne utvrđuje što je bilo grješno; odlomak ne daje pojedinosti koje bi opravdale takav zaključak.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusov poziv „Obratite se i vjerujte Evanđelju” povezuje obraćenje s okretanjem od zla prema Bogu, a ne s pukim odbacivanjem određenog načina života ili materijalnih stvari. Katekizam obraćenje opisuje kao žaljenje zbog počinjenih grijeha i čvrstu odluku da ih se ubuduće ne čini, uz nadu u Božje milosrđe; ono zato može uključivati snažnu životnu prekretnicu, ali i trajni rast.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage presents a personal testimony about moving away from God and does not claim that worldly amusement itself or possessing things is necessarily a sin. His account is largely compatible with Christian discourse on conversion, but the claim that the life of „every convert” is divided into a period before and after meeting Christ may overly simplify the diverse paths of conversion.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' call to „Repent and believe in the Gospel” connects conversion with turning away from evil toward God, and not with the mere rejection of a particular way of life or material things. The Catechism describes conversion as sorrow for committed sins and a firm resolution not to commit them in the future, with hope in God's mercy; it can therefore involve a powerful life turning point, but also ongoing growth.
concerns_en: The expression that the life of every convert is divided into two parts may suggest an equally sudden or dramatic pattern for everyone; Church teaching recognizes foundational turning points, but also gradual and daily conversion.
The description of partying, sports, money, a car, and a motorbike does not in itself determine what was sinful; the passage does not provide details that would justify such a conclusion.

sections.subtitle_en: Life without God: parties, a motorbike, and an ever deeper emptiness
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the feeling of loneliness and emptiness during the period without God
sections.content_en:
The host recalls that the life of every convert is divided into two parts, before and after meeting Christ, and asks what the guest's life looked like before his conversion.

Krznarić calls this a „classic“. He received all the sacraments on time, and then puberty came and faith became a „burden“ to him. In 1993, at 21 years of age, **he rejected God**. He began to think and live worldly: he partied, actively engaged in sports, had his own money, a car, and a motorbike. From the outside, all of this, he says, „looked nice“.

That phase lasted only a few months, about half a year. Alongside worldly pleasure, he increasingly felt **loneliness and emptiness**. He admits that his faith had earlier also been more „pro forma“, out of tradition and upbringing, without true fervor. Nevertheless, that faith obviously meant a lot to him, because without it „something was missing“.

The turning point was **a major confession with fra Ante Barišić** that lasted an hour. When he received absolution, from him, as he describes, „a huge mud fell off“ and he walked out „like a new man“. From that moment, he says, he strives to live „with full lungs for the Lord“.

sections.subtitle: Sandra, „moj bingo“: kako je ponizno priznanje vratilo izgubljenu ljubav
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava kako je Sandri došao „mali kao makovo zrno“ priznati pogrešku
sections.content:
Voditelj zatim pita za vezu koja je postojala prije te ispovijedi i nastavila se nakon nje. Krznarić kaže da je „veliki sretnik“ jer ima Sandru, ženu koja je od njega „učinila i oca i muža“ i uz koju se ostvario u mnogim područjima.

Njih su dvoje dvije godine hodali „na svjetovan način“, a onda ju je on ostavio. Bila je lijepa, pametna i dobra, ali on, kako priznaje, „nije imao žar“. Uslijedila je faza bez Boga u kojoj je imao druge djevojke.

Nakon ispovijedi napravio je „totalni reset“. Više nije izlazio, nego je usred dana odlazio na pola sata u crkvu na „čvenk s Gospodinom“ umjesto u kafić s društvom. Kroz duhovne obnove i molitvu shvatio je da je Sandra bila **najbolja osoba u njegovu životu**, njegov „bingo“.

Sandri je došao, kako sam kaže, *„kao najmanji od najmanjih, mali kao makovo zrno“*. Rekao joj je da je bio slijep i da je pogriješio. Dodao je da od nje ništa ne traži, pa ni da ga pozdravi ili ostane s njim u prijateljstvu, nego samo želi da to zna.

Sandra je u to vrijeme razlučivala hoće li postati časna sestra ili se udati. Čudila se njegovu dolasku jer je za nju „to bila završena priča“. Bojala se da je „lud“, iako ga je viđala u crkvi. S vremenom su ipak ponovno postali prijatelji, a zatim su opet počeli hodati. *„Ta se šansa isplatila“*, zaključuje Krznarić. Danas imaju petero djece, tri sina i dvije kćeri.

magisterium.assessment: Zahvalnost prema supruzi i priznanje vlastitog ranijeg prekida veze ne proturječe katoličkom nauku; riječ je ponajprije o osobnom svjedočanstvu, a ne o izričitoj teološkoj tvrdnji. Budući da se odlomak prekida nakon riječi „imao...”, nije moguće procijeniti nastavak niti utvrditi kako se dogodilo pomirenje.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk povezuje ljubav u obitelji s poniznošću, služenjem i opraštanjem, a ne s nadmetanjem ili dominacijom (Mt 20,26–27; 1 Pt 5,5). Pomirenje je povezano s obraćenjem srca, dok se za kršćanski brak posebno ističu vjernost savezu i snaga Božje milosti; no dostupni odlomak ne daje dovoljno pojedinosti da bi se procijenilo kako se ta gledišta odnose na njihovu situaciju.

citations.document_title: Amoris Laetitia
Gratissimam Sane: Letter to Families
Reconciliatio et Paenitentia

magisterium.assessment_en: Gratitude toward one's wife and the admission of one's own earlier breakup of a relationship do not contradict Catholic teaching; it is primarily a matter of personal testimony rather than an explicit theological claim. Since the excerpt cuts off after the words “he had...”, it is not possible to assess the continuation or determine how the reconciliation occurred.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching links love in the family with humility, service, and forgiveness, rather than with competition or domination (Mt 20:26–27; 1 Pet 5:5). Reconciliation is linked to the conversion of heart, while for Christian marriage, fidelity to the covenant and the power of God's grace are especially emphasized; however, the available excerpt does not provide enough details to assess how these perspectives apply to their situation.

sections.subtitle_en: Sandra, “my bingo”: how a humble confession brought back lost love
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts how he came to Sandra “as small as a poppy seed” to admit his mistake
sections.content_en:
The host then asks about the relationship that existed before that confession and continued after it. Krznarić says that he is “very fortunate” because he has Sandra, a woman who “made both a father and a husband” out of him and alongside whom he found fulfillment in many areas.

The two of them dated for two years “in a worldly way,” and then he left her. She was beautiful, smart, and good, but he, as he admits, “did not have the zeal.” A phase without God followed, in which he had other girlfriends.

After confession, he did a “total reset.” He no longer went out; instead, in the middle of the day, he would go to church for half an hour for a “date with the Lord” instead of going to a cafe with friends. Through spiritual retreats and prayer, he realized that Sandra was **the best person in his life**, his “bingo.”

He came to Sandra, as he himself says, *“like the least of the least, as small as a poppy seed”*. He told her that he had been blind and that he had made a mistake. He added that he was not asking anything of her, not even to greet him or remain in friendship with him, but only wanted her to know that.

Sandra was discerning at that time whether to become a nun or get married. She was surprised by his arrival because for her “it was a finished story.” She was afraid that he was “crazy,” even though she used to see him in church. Over time, however, they became friends again, and then they started dating again. *“That chance paid off”*, Krznarić concludes. Today they have five children, three sons and two daughters.

sections.subtitle: Tri godine u čistoći, brak 1998. i prijevara koja je odnijela sve
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje kako ih je investitor na Krku prevario i kako je ostao bez svega
sections.content:
Krznarić naglašava pojedinost koju voditelj spominje: sa Sandrom je **tri godine hodao u čistoći**. Prije su, kaže, „probali sve što svijet nudi“ i shvatili da „to nije to“. U čistoći je otkrio njezinu unutarnju ljepotu. To je ono „od čega se živi“, „ono što traje“, korijen i temelj na koji se kasnije može osloniti, jer je tu savez između Boga i njih dvoje.

Vjenčali su se **1998. godine**. Život se razvijao lijepo: posao, obitelj, sve je „išlo super“. Krznarić je sa skupinom ulagača sav novac uložio u gradnju nekretnina. Prva zgrada na **Pagu** donijela je lijepu zaradu. Sljedeći projekt na **Krku** završio je katastrofom jer ih je, kako kaže, jedan čovjek prevario i ostali su bez svega.

Detalje naziva „kompliciranom pričom“ i ne ulazi u njih. Opisuje samo svoje stanje: s 39 godina osjećao se *„opljačkan, dužan, prevaren“*.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na trogodišnjem hodanju u čistoći i otkrivanju karaktera druge osobe uglavnom je usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem zaruka kao vremena sazrijevanja i pripreme za bračni dar sebe. Ipak, izraz da je već tada postojao savez između Boga i njih dvoje može zamagliti razliku između pobožnog hodanja i ženidbenog saveza, koji nastaje sklapanjem ženidbe.
concerns: Nije jasno znači li izraz „probali sve što svijet nudi” da su prije toga imali spolne odnose; bez dodatnog konteksta ne treba pretpostaviti što se dogodilo. Ako se odnosi na spolne odnose prije ženidbe, oni nisu u skladu s katoličkim naukom o čistoći, premda kasniji izbor čistoće predstavlja dobar smjer obraćenja.
Govor o savezu Boga i para tijekom hodanja može se razumjeti kao duhovna orijentacija njihove veze, ali ne bi ga trebalo poistovjetiti sa sakramentalnim ženidbenim savezom.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva čistoću ne shvaća kao odbacivanje ljubavi, nego kao krepost koja pomaže poštovati dostojanstvo druge osobe i priprema zaručnike za vjernost i uzajamni dar u ženidbi. Papa Franjo posebno ističe da zaruke i ženidba nisu isto te da je vrijeme zaruka put sazrijevanja prije ženidbenog obećanja. Stoga je najpreciznije razumjeti njihovo hodanje u čistoći kao pripravu za ženidbeni savez sklopljen 1998., a ne kao sam taj savez.

citations.document_title: Catechumenal Pathways for Married Life
citations.document_author: Dicastery for Laity, Family and Life

citations.document_title: General Audience of 27 May 2015: The family - 16. Engagement
Meeting with the youth in Nakivubo Stadium in Kampala (February 6, 1993) - Speech

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on three years of dating in purity and discovering the character of the other person is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding of engagement as a time of maturation and preparation for the marital gift of self. Nevertheless, the expression that a covenant between God and the two of them already existed then can blur the distinction between pious dating and the marital covenant, which comes into being through the contracting of marriage.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church does not understand purity as a rejection of love, but as a virtue that helps respect the dignity of the other person and prepares engaged couples for fidelity and mutual gift in marriage. Pope Francis especially emphasizes that engagement and marriage are not the same and that the time of engagement is a path of maturation before the marital promise. Therefore, it is most precise to understand their dating in purity as preparation for the marital covenant entered into in 1998, and not as that covenant itself.
concerns_en: It is not clear whether the expression „tried everything the world offers” means that they had sexual relations prior to that; without additional context one should not assume what happened. If it refers to sexual relations before marriage, they are not in accordance with Catholic teaching on purity, although the later choice of purity represents a good direction of conversion.
Speaking of a covenant of God and the couple during dating can be understood as the spiritual orientation of their relationship, but it should not be equated with the sacramental marital covenant.

sections.subtitle_en: Three years in purity, marriage in 1998, and a fraud that took everything away
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes how an investor on Krk defrauded them and how he was left with nothing
sections.content_en:
Krznarić emphasizes a detail mentioned by the host: with Sandra he **dated in purity for three years**. Before that, he says, they had „tried everything the world offers“ and realized that „that is not it“. In purity he discovered her inner beauty. That is what „one lives on“, „what lasts“, the root and foundation upon which one can rely later, because there is a covenant between God and the two of them.

They got married **in 1998**. Life developed nicely: work, family, everything „went great“. Krznarić, with a group of investors, invested all the money into real estate construction. The first building on **Pag** brought a nice profit. The next project on **Krk** ended in disaster because, as he says, one man defrauded them and they were left with nothing.

He calls the details a „complicated story“ and does not go into them. He describes only his own state: at 39 years old he felt *„robbed, indebted, cheated“*.

sections.subtitle: Stečaj, a tri tjedna kasnije nesreća kilometar od kuće
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava nesreću na zaleđenom mostiću 2011. godine
sections.content:
Nevolje su se nizale. Nakon prijevare uslijedio je **stečaj**, a dva do tri tjedna kasnije, 2011. godine, Krznarić je doživio prometnu nesreću. Dogodila se samo kilometar od kuće, na cesti kojom se vozio svakodnevno i na kojoj je „napamet znao svaki kamen“.

Na zaleđenom mostiću automobil se zavrtio, a kad se zaustavio, u njega je udarila gospođa i priklještila mu obje noge. Desna je spašena, a **lijeva je amputirana**.

U bolnici je, kako opisuje, bio „dužan, slomljen, opljačkan, bez zdravlja“. Pitao je: *„Bože, pa zašto? Bože, gdje si? Zašto si dopustio sve ovo tako odjedanput? Sa svih strana me tučeš.“* Sve se dogodilo iznenada, a on tri dana nije mogao spavati.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom jer opisuje financijski gubitak, nesreću, amputaciju i krizu vjere kao životne događaje, bez tvrdnje da su kazna za grijeh ili znak Božje napuštenosti. Budući da ne iznosi izričitu teološku tvrdnju, njegova usklađenost prvenstveno proizlazi iz toga što ne proturječi vjeri.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk razlikuje fizičko zlo, poput ozljede i bolesti, od moralnog zla; fizička patnja ne znači nužno osobnu krivnju niti sama po sebi otkriva zašto se dogodila. Kršćanska vjera ne poriče da patnja može izazvati sumnju i teška pitanja, nego govori o Bogu koji čovjeka prati i u boli, premda njezin smisao nije uvijek moguće jasno razabrati u trenutku kušnje.

citations.document_title: General Audience of 4 June 1986
Acta Apostolicae Sedis: Issue 2, February, 2005
To sick, elderly and handicapped people in Wellington (November 23, 1986) - Speech

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching because it describes financial loss, an accident, an amputation, and a crisis of faith as life events, without claiming that they are a punishment for sin or a sign of God's abandonment. Since it does not make an explicit theological claim, its alignment primarily stems from the fact that it does not contradict the faith.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching distinguishes physical evil, such as injury and illness, from moral evil; physical suffering does not necessarily mean personal guilt, nor does it in itself reveal why it happened. The Christian faith does not deny that suffering can provoke doubt and difficult questions, but speaks of a God who accompanies man even in pain, although its meaning cannot always be clearly discerned in the moment of temptation.

sections.subtitle_en: Bankruptcy, and three weeks later an accident a kilometer from home
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts the accident on an icy bridge in 2011
sections.content_en:
Troubles followed one after another. After the fraud followed **bankruptcy**, and two to three weeks later, in 2011, Krznarić suffered a traffic accident. It happened just a kilometer from home, on a road he drove every day and on which he „knew every stone by heart”.

On an icy bridge the car spun around, and when it stopped, a lady struck it and crushed both of his legs. The right one was saved, and **the left one was amputated**.

In the hospital, as he describes, he was „in debt, broken, robbed, without health”. He asked: *„God, why? God, where are you? Why did you allow all of this so all at once? You are striking me from all sides.”* Everything happened suddenly, and for three days he could not sleep.

sections.subtitle: „Ja bum ga rodila“: Sandrina vjera kao planina
sections.screenshot_description: Gost s emocijom prenosi Sandrine riječi o trudnoći s petim djetetom
sections.content:
Krznarić se osjećao slomljeno i, kako kaže, kao u „pat poziciji“: nije se imao za što primiti i bio je satjeran u kut. Tada mu je u bolnicu došla supruga i rekla: *„Zlatko, trudna sam dva mjeseca s našim petim djetetom, s našim Leom.“*

Financijska slika bila je teška. On je jedini zarađivao, a Sandra je bila kućanica. Imali su kredit u švicarskim francima, za koji voditelj ironično dobacuje da je bio „jako isplativ“. Pod hipotekom su bile i njihova kuća i kuća njegovih roditelja. Čak i da se Sandra zaposlila, ne bi bilo dovoljno za ratu.

Tada ga je Sandra primila za ruku i rekla:

> *„Evo, taman da smo sad tak siromašni da nikada više nećemo ništa imati i da nam zbog našeg siromaštva socijalna služba mora to dijete uzeti, ja bum ga rodila. Ja sam mu majka. Dala bum mu život jer Bog ima plan za nas.“*

Krznarić kaže da mu je upravo to bilo „najpotrebnije“. U njoj je vidio hrabrost, odanost i vjeru koja je bila „planina“, i to ga je silno ohrabrilo.

magisterium.assessment: Prikaz Sandrine vjere i spremnosti da prihvati trudnoću unatoč ozbiljnim financijskim teškoćama u skladu je s katoličkim poštovanjem života i otvorenošću bračnog zajedništva daru djece. Odlomak je svjedočanstveni, a ne cjelovit moralno-teološki prikaz, pa sam po sebi ne razjašnjava kako supružnici promišljaju odgovorno roditeljstvo.
concerns: Ne bi trebalo zaključiti da katolički nauk zahtijeva neograničen broj djece ili zanemarivanje sposobnosti roditelja da se brinu za obitelj: odgovorna odluka o roditeljstvu uključuje razborito razmatranje okolnosti, odgovornosti prema već rođenoj djeci i pravilno oblikovane savjesti.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička vjera poziva bračne drugove da život prihvate kao Božji dar: Sveto pismo naziva djecu „baštinom Gospodnjom“ (Ps 127,3), a crkveno učenje naglašava da roditelji sudjeluju u Božjem stvarateljskom djelu. Istodobno, odgovorno roditeljstvo traži zajedničko, savjesno razlučivanje koje uzima u obzir stvarne obiteljske okolnosti, a ne samo financijski strah niti nekritičko zanemarivanje obveza skrbi i odgoja.

citations.document_title: Acta Apostolicae Sedis: Issue 5, May, 1995
Acta Apostolicae Sedis: Issue 5, May, 1995
The Foundations of the Church's Doctrine Concerning the Principles of Conjugal Life: A memorandum composed by a group of moral theologians from Kraków

magisterium.assessment_en: The portrayal of Sandra's faith and willingness to accept pregnancy despite serious financial difficulties is in accordance with the Catholic respect for life and the openness of the marital union to the gift of children. The passage is testimonial rather than a complete moral-theological presentation, so in itself it does not clarify how spouses discern responsible parenthood.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic faith calls spouses to accept life as God's gift: Sacred Scripture calls children a “heritage from the Lord” (Ps 127:3), and Church teaching emphasizes that parents participate in God's creative work. At the same time, responsible parenthood requires a joint, conscientious discernment that takes into account real family circumstances, and not merely financial fear nor an uncritical neglect of the obligations of care and upbringing.
concerns_en: It should not be concluded that Catholic teaching requires an unlimited number of children or the neglect of parents' ability to care for the family: a responsible decision about parenthood includes a prudent consideration of circumstances, responsibilities toward children already born, and a properly formed conscience.

sections.subtitle_en: “I'm going to give birth to him”: Sandra's faith like a mountain
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest emotionally conveys Sandra's words about the pregnancy with their fifth child
sections.content_en:
Krznarić felt broken and, as he says, in a “stalemate”: he had nothing to hold onto and was backed into a corner. Then his wife came to him at the hospital and said: *“Zlatko, I am two months pregnant with our fifth child, with our Leo.”*

The financial picture was difficult. He was the sole earner, and Sandra was a homemaker. They had a loan in Swiss francs, about which the host ironically quips that it was “very profitable.” Both their house and his parents' house were mortgaged. Even if Sandra had gotten a job, it would not have been enough for the installment.

Then Sandra took him by the hand and said:

> *“Look, even if we are so poor right now that we will never have anything again and that because of our poverty social services must take that child away from us, I'm going to give birth to him. I am his mother. I will give him life because God has a plan for us.”*

Krznarić says that this was precisely what was “most needed” for him. In her he saw courage, devotion, and a faith that was a “mountain,” and that encouraged him immensely.

sections.subtitle: Kapelan koji se smijao: „To je prava stvar!“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prenosi proročke riječi bolničkog kapelana vlč. Milana Lončarića
sections.content:
Ubrzo ga je posjetio bolnički kapelan, **vlč. Milan Lončarić**. Krznarić mu je nabrajao svoje nevolje, a kapelan se, na njegovo čuđenje, sve više smijao. Kad mu je rekao da mu osiguravatelj nije stigao uplatiti kasko policu od oko dva i pol milijuna kuna, pa je ostao bez ičega, svećenik je uzviknuo: *„To je prava stvar!“*

Krznarić se pitao je li kapelan „normalan“. Tada je čuo riječi koje danas naziva **proročkima**:

> *„Zlatko, do sad si mogao biti katolik na papiru, ali, evo, danas te Bog zove da mu predaš svoj život. Ako si to spreman učiniti, pisat ćeš o njemu, svjedočit ćeš. Imat ćeš pravu radost koja ne visi o tvome novcu i zdravlju.“*

Kapelan mu je kasnije priznao da uopće nije bio svjestan što govori, a Krznarić je uvjeren da ga je tada obuzeo Duh Sveti. Otišao je u bolničku kapelicu i **predao svoj život Bogu**. Spustio se na njega, kaže, „predivan mir“, kao da je s Bogom sklopio najvažniji ugovor „bez tinte i papira“.

Kasnije se sve posložilo „na najbolji mogući način“. Uz Božju pomoć, kako kaže „na nadnaravan način“, obitelj je odavno vratila sve dugove. *„Danas sam sretan čovjek. Bog je živ“*, poručuje.

magisterium.assessment: Prikaz svećenikova ohrabrenja i mogućeg duhovnog obrata može biti u skladu s kršćanskim razumijevanjem obraćenja, ali ulomak ne daje dovoljno konteksta da bi se procijenilo zašto je gubitak novca nazvan „pravom stvari“. Nazivanje riječi „proročkima“ ostaje osobno tumačenje, a ne potvrda nadnaravnog podrijetla.
concerns: Izvan konteksta, odgovor može zvučati kao da su nesreća i financijski gubitak sami po sebi dobri ili poželjni; kršćansko prihvaćanje patnje ne znači da zlo ili gubitak treba smatrati dobrom.
Tvrdnja o proroštvu ne može se provjeriti jer je citat prekinut, a nadnaravne tvrdnje zahtijevaju razborito crkveno razlučivanje.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanin može vjerovati da Bog iz teških okolnosti izvodi duhovno dobro, ali to nije isto što i tvrditi da je sama šteta bila dobra ili da je njezin nastup izravno objavljen od Boga. Crkvene smjernice za razlučivanje navodnih nadnaravnih pojava traže, među ostalim, pravovjernost poruke i dobre duhovne plodove, dok je objavljena Riječ u Kristu dostatna za kršćanski život.

citations.document_author: Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith

citations.document_title: Norms for Proceeding in the Discernment of Alleged Supernatural Phenomena
citations.document_author: Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith

magisterium.assessment_en: The presentation of the priest's encouragement and a possible spiritual turnaround can be in accordance with the Christian understanding of conversion, but the excerpt does not provide enough context to assess why the loss of money was called "the real thing". Calling the words "prophetic" remains a personal interpretation, not a confirmation of supernatural origin.
magisterium.enrichment_en: A Christian may believe that God brings spiritual good out of difficult circumstances, but that is not the same as claiming that the harm itself was good or that its occurrence was directly revealed by God. Church guidelines for the discernment of alleged supernatural phenomena require, among other things, the orthodoxy of the message and good spiritual fruits, while the revealed Word in Christ is sufficient for Christian life.
concerns_en: Out of context, the response may sound as if misfortune and financial loss are good or desirable in themselves; Christian acceptance of suffering does not mean that evil or loss should be considered a good.
The claim of prophecy cannot be verified because the quote is broken off, and supernatural claims require prudent ecclesial discernment.

sections.subtitle_en: The chaplain who laughed: "That's the real thing!"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest conveys the prophetic words of hospital chaplain Fr. Milan Lončarić
sections.content_en:
Soon he was visited by the hospital chaplain, **Fr. Milan Lončarić**. Krznarić listed his troubles to him, and the chaplain, to his astonishment, laughed more and more. When he told him that the insurer had not managed to pay out his comprehensive car insurance policy of about two and a half million kunas, leaving him with nothing, the priest exclaimed: *"That's the real thing!"*

Krznarić wondered if the chaplain was "normal". Then he heard the words that he today calls **prophetic**:

> *"Zlatko, until now you could have been a Catholic on paper, but, behold, today God is calling you to surrender your life to Him. If you are ready to do that, you will write about Him, you will witness. You will have true joy that does not hang on your money and health."*

The chaplain later admitted to him that he was not at all aware of what he was saying, and Krznarić is convinced that the Holy Spirit overtook him then. He went to the hospital chapel and **surrendered his life to God**. A "wonderful peace" descended upon him, he says, as if he had made the most important contract with God "without ink and paper".

Later, everything fell into place "in the best possible way". With God's help, as he says "in a supernatural way", the family long ago repaid all debts. *"Today I am a happy man. God is alive"*, he sends as a message.

sections.subtitle: „Ti si svjedok“: knjiga koju najlošiji učenik dvije godine nije htio napisati
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje svoju borbu s poticajem „Napiši knjigu!“
sections.content:
Kapelanove riječi su se obistinile. Godine **2017.** izašla je Krznarićeva prva knjiga, **„Ti si svjedok“**. Voditelj je naziva uspješnicom s kojom je autor obišao cijelu državu i šire te tvrdi da se nalazi „u gotovo svakom katoličkom domu“. I sam ima primjerak s autorovim potpisom, ali ga je zaboravio ponijeti na snimanje.

Krznarić se najprije javno zahvaljuje voditelju što mu je napravio **lekturu** i šali se da zbog toga kod Gospodina ide „među svece i mučenike“. Voditelj odgovara da je „bilo posla, ali bio je gušt“. Gost pritom sebe naziva „polupismenim“.

Priznaje da kapelanovo „pisat ćeš o njemu“ isprva nije shvatio ozbiljno. Nakon nekog vremena, kad je u crkvi pitao Boga što može učiniti za njega, dobio je odgovor: *„Napiši knjigu!“* Slijedila je borba duga nešto manje od dvije godine. Bio je, kaže, jedan od najgorih učenika u školi i nije mogao zamisliti da sjedne za stol i piše. Pitao se i tko bi to uopće čitao.

Rezultat ga je iznenadio: knjiga je imala **četiri izdanja, prodana je u tisućama primjeraka i prevedena je**. Vjeruje da je čitateljima dirnula iskrenost. U knjizi je, kaže, „ogolio sebe do kraja“, pišući o slabostima, svađama i intimi. *„Svi smo negdje tanki, svi imamo nešto što nas žulja“*, objašnjava. Nije želio pisati ništa veliko o sebi, nego koliko je on slab, a Bog velik kroz njegove slabosti. Bog je, kaže, uvijek vjeran, a pitanje je samo jesmo li mi.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ne iznosi izričit teološki nauk; šala o odlasku „među svece i mučenike” djeluje kao zahvalna dosjetka, a ne kao tvrdnja da je lektura sama po sebi zasluga za svetost ili mučeništvo. Ipak, izvadak je prekinut usred rečenice, pa se ne može procijeniti ostatak razgovora ni širi kontekst šale.
concerns: Ako bi se izraz shvatio doslovno ili ponavljao bez osjetljivosti, mogao bi umanjiti ozbiljnost svetosti i mučeništva; u prikazanom kontekstu nema jasnog pokazatelja da je to namjera.
magisterium.enrichment: U katoličkom nauku svetost je poziv svih krštenih i očituje se u vjernom življenju ljubavi u svakodnevnim okolnostima, a ne samo u izvanrednim djelima. Mučeništvo je osobito svjedočenje Kristu, pa ga valja razlikovati od šaljive usporedbe ili obične pohvale.

sections.subtitle_en: "You Are a Witness": The Book That the Worst Student Did Not Want to Write for Two Years
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes his struggle with the prompt "Write a book!"
sections.content_en:
The chaplain's words came true. In the year **2017**, Krznarić's first book, **"You Are a Witness"**, was released. The host calls it a bestseller with which the author toured the entire country and beyond, asserting that it is found "in almost every Catholic home." He himself owns a copy signed by the author, but forgot to bring it to the recording.

Krznarić first publicly thanks the host for doing the **proofreading** for him and jokes that because of this, with the Lord, he goes "among the saints and martyrs." The host responds that "it was work, but it was a pleasure." In doing so, the guest calls himself "semi-literate."

He admits that he did not take the chaplain's "you will write about him" seriously at first. After some time, when he asked God in church what he could do for Him, he received the answer: *"Write a book!"* A struggle lasting just under two years followed. He was, he says, one of the worst students in school and could not imagine sitting down at a desk and writing. He also wondered who would read it at all.

The result surprised him: the book had **four editions, was sold in thousands of copies, and was translated**. He believes that the honesty touched the readers. In the book, he says, he "stripped himself down completely," writing about weaknesses, quarrels, and intimate matters. *"We are all thin somewhere, we all have something that pinches us,"* he explains. He did not want to write anything great about himself, but rather how weak he is, and how great God is through his weaknesses. God is, he says, always faithful, and the only question is whether we are.

sections.subtitle: Olovka u Božjim rukama i tiskar koji ne vjeruje nakladama
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava kako nije prepoznao vlastiti tekst kad ga je svećenik čitao
sections.content:
Na pitanje o najdražem poglavlju Krznarić govori o samom procesu pisanja. Često nije mogao dovršiti zaključak svjedočanstva, nekoliko završnih rečenica, sve dok mu nakon molitve i predanja nisu „došle riječi“.

Jednom ga je svećenik pozvao u župu da svjedoči i pročitao ulomak iz njegove knjige. Krznarić je slušao i mislio: *„Gle, kak je ovo lijepo rekao!“* Tek je poslije shvatio da je to njegov tekst. Zaboravio ga je jer, kako kaže, „nije bilo moje“. Zahvaljuje Bogu „na suradnji“ i na nadahnuću.

Zabavna je i priča o tiskaru. Kad je pitao Boga koliko primjeraka tiskati, dobivao je brojke od nekoliko tisuća. Vlasnik tiskare, nevjernik, čudio se: *„Tko si ti?“* Krznarić mu je odgovorio da je „nitko i ništa“, ali da Onaj koji ga je potaknuo „drži svijet u ruci“.

I danas tiska kod istog čovjeka. Tiskar se, kaže, nije obratio, ali mu govori: *„Ti nisi uračunljiv, ti si van svih standarda.“* Pred petim izdanjem Krznarić se opet „boji pitati“ Boga za brojku. Sebe opisuje kao „samo olovku u Njegovim rukama“.

magisterium.assessment: Opis da su mu nakon molitve došle riječi i da zahvaljuje Bogu na suradnji uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim razumijevanjem molitve, milosti i Božje providnosti. Izraz „nije bilo moje” može se razumjeti kao ponizno priznanje Božje pomoći, ali iz isječka nije jasno misli li time na duhovno nadahnuće u širem smislu ili na nadahnuće Svetoga pisma, što bi bilo posebno i ne treba ih poistovjećivati.
concerns: Moguća je nejasnoća ako se osobni doživljaj nadahnuća pri pisanju knjige shvati kao istovjetan božanskom nadahnuću Svetoga pisma.
Izraz „nije bilo moje” ne bi trebalo tumačiti kao poricanje vlastitog stvarnog autorstva ili odgovornosti za napisani tekst.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko učenje o nadahnuću Svetoga pisma ne opisuje ga kao puku diktaciju: Bog djeluje, a ljudski pisci ostaju autentični autori. Molitva može čovjeka otvoriti djelovanju Duha Svetoga i pomoći mu u stvaralačkom radu, no takvo osobno iskustvo samo po sebi ne čini tekst Svetim pismom niti ga stavlja na istu razinu autoriteta.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description that the words came to him after prayer and that he thanks God for cooperation is largely in accordance with the Catholic understanding of prayer, grace, and God's providence. The expression "it was not mine" can be understood as a humble acknowledgment of God's help, but from the clip it is not clear whether by this he means spiritual inspiration in a broader sense or the inspiration of Sacred Scripture, which would be distinct and they should not be equated.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching on the inspiration of Sacred Scripture does not describe it as mere dictation: God acts, and the human writers remain authentic authors. Prayer can open a person to the action of the Holy Spirit and help him in creative work, but such personal experience in itself does not make the text Sacred Scripture nor does it place it at the same level of authority.
concerns_en: Ambiguity is possible if the personal experience of inspiration when writing a book is understood as identical to the divine inspiration of Sacred Scripture.
The expression "it was not mine" should not be interpreted as a denial of one's own actual authorship or responsibility for the written text.

sections.subtitle_en: A pencil in God's hands and a printer who does not believe the print runs
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts how he did not recognize his own text when a priest was reading it
sections.content_en:
To the question about his favorite chapter, Krznarić speaks about the writing process itself. Often he could not finish the conclusion of a testimony, a few final sentences, until after prayer and surrender the "words came" to him.

Once a priest invited him to the parish to give witness and read an excerpt from his book. Krznarić listened and thought: *"Look, how beautifully he said this!"* Only later did he realize that it was his own text. He had forgotten it because, as he says, "it was not mine". He thanks God "for the cooperation" and for the inspiration.

The story about the printer is also entertaining. When he asked God how many copies to print, he received figures of several thousand. The print shop owner, an unbeliever, was astonished: *"Who are you?"* Krznarić replied to him that he was "nobody and nothing", but that the One who prompted him "holds the world in his hand".

Even today he prints with the same man. The printer, he says, has not converted, but tells him: *"You are not sane, you are beyond all standards."* Before the fifth edition, Krznarić is again "afraid to ask" God for the number. He describes himself as "just a pencil in His hands".

sections.subtitle: Napad na molitelje i molitva koja je slomila agresivno srce
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava zašto je zajednica odlučila moliti za čovjeka koji ga je napao
sections.content:
Voditeljevo najdraže svjedočanstvo iz knjige vezano je uz inicijativu **„40 dana za život“**. Krznarić je bio na ručku kod majke, juha je već bila u tanjuru, kad je osjetio poticaj da izađe van. *„Gospodine, pa jedem, kaj sad?“* pitao je, ali je izašao.

Pred molitelje je automobilom došao čovjek i počeo ih agresivno vrijeđati. Krznarić ga je počeo snimati mobitelom. Kad je čovjek to primijetio, pitao ga je tko je i zašto snima, a zatim ga je **počeo daviti**. Krznarić se oslobodio, napadač je otišao, a policija je napravila očevid jer se napad dogodio na javnom mjestu.

Zajednica je potom odlučila **moliti za napadača**. U tome Krznarić vidi „poantu Božje pedagogije“: nisu uzvratili, nisu išli „na mišiće“, nego „na Božji način“. Nakon nekog vremena čovjek je župniku uplatio prilog za crkvu, nazvao Krznarića i zamolio ga za oprost. *„Njegovo srce se slomilo. Ono agresivno počelo je biti ljudsko, počelo je biti Božje“*, kaže. Taj događaj naziva „prstom Božjim“ i zato ga je uvrstio u knjigu.

magisterium.assessment: Prikaz molitelja koji su izloženi vrijeđanju i napadu, u kontekstu molitve za neprijatelja, oprosta i obraćenja, načelno je u skladu s Isusovim pozivom da se moli za progonitelje i odgovara na zlo dobrom. Budući da je odlomak prekinut, nije moguće procijeniti kako je Krznarić reagirao tijekom napada ni je li prikaz događaja izveden kao pouka o nenasilju i oprostu.
concerns: Odlomak završava usred rečenice, pa ne pokazuje je li odgovor na napad bio nenasilan, je li uslijedila molitva ili oprost, niti što se podrazumijeva pod tvrdnjom da je molitva slomila agresivno srce.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusov nalog da se ljubi neprijatelje i moli za progonitelje postavlja molitvu i oprost kao kršćanski odgovor, a ne osvetu; Katekizam ističe da oprost svjedoči kako je ljubav jača od grijeha. To ne znači pasivno odobravanje nasilja: kršćansko nenasilje odgovara na zlo dobrom i istinom te nastoji prekinuti krug neprijateljstva. (Mt 5,44; Rim 12,17–21)

magisterium.assessment_en: The depiction of prayer intercessors who are subjected to insults and an attack, in the context of prayer for enemies, forgiveness, and conversion, is in principle in accordance with Jesus' call to pray for persecutors and respond to evil with good. Since the passage is cut off, it is not possible to assess how Krznarić reacted during the attack or whether the depiction of the event was presented as a lesson on nonviolence and forgiveness.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' command to love enemies and pray for persecutors establishes prayer and forgiveness as the Christian response, not revenge; the Catechism emphasizes that forgiveness bears witness that love is stronger than sin. This does not mean passive approval of violence: Christian nonviolence responds to evil with good and truth and seeks to break the cycle of hostility. (Mt 5:44; Rom 12:17–21)
concerns_en: The passage ends in the middle of a sentence, so it does not show whether the response to the attack was nonviolent, whether prayer or forgiveness followed, nor what is meant by the claim that prayer broke an aggressive heart.

sections.subtitle_en: Attack on Prayer Intercessors and the Prayer That Broke an Aggressive Heart
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains why the community decided to pray for the man who attacked him
sections.content_en:
The host's favorite testimony from the book is related to the **"40 Days for Life"** initiative. Krznarić was having lunch at his mother's, the soup was already in the plate, when he felt an urge to go outside. *"Lord, but I am eating, what now?"* he asked, but he went outside.

A man arrived by car in front of the prayer intercessors and began aggressively insulting them. Krznarić began recording him with a mobile phone. When the man noticed this, he asked him who he was and why he was recording, and then **started choking him**. Krznarić broke free, the attacker left, and the police conducted an investigation because the attack took place in a public place.

The community then decided **to pray for the attacker**. In this, Krznarić sees the "point of God's pedagogy": they did not retaliate, they did not go "by muscle," but "God's way." After some time, the man gave a contribution for the church to the parish priest, called Krznarić, and asked him for forgiveness. *"His heart broke. That aggressive part began to be human, began to be God's,"* he says. He calls that event the "finger of God" and that is why he included it in the book.

sections.subtitle: Govor na prvoj pričesti i neočekivani poziv: „Redimo te za đakona“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava reakciju župnika i kapelana nakon govora na sinovoj prvoj pričesti
sections.content:
Voditelj primjećuje da Krznarića posljednje četiri godine gotovo nema u javnosti i pita gdje je bio. Odgovor glasi: **dobio je poziv za trajnog đakona.**

Nije ni znao da trajni đakonat postoji niti ga je to ikad zanimalo. Kad mu je sin išao na prvu pričest, župnik je tražio nekoga od roditelja da održi govor. Nitko se nije javio, pa je župnik rekao: „Ajde, budeš ti, Zlatko.“ Govorio je „po Duhu“, a čim je završio, prišli su mu kapelan i župnik: *„Redimo te za đakona!“*

Nasmijao se i rekao im neka rede nekog drugog. No u molitvi mu se ta misao stalno vraćala. Nije znao da oženjen čovjek može služiti blizu oltara, pa se počeo raspitivati.

U razgovoru navodi da je jedan od najpoznatijih đakona **sveti Franjo**, koji se iz poniznosti nije usudio postati svećenikom. Za oženjenog kandidata postoje ovi uvjeti:

- mora biti stariji od 35 godina,
- supruga mora dati pristanak,
- mora završiti **pet godina teološkog studija**.

Prva dva uvjeta nisu bila problem, ali treći ga je prestrašio: *„Ma koji faks? Pa nikad nisam bio za školu!“*

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem da se đakonski poziv može prepoznati kroz služenje zajednici i poticaj župnika, ali pripovijest sama po sebi ne potvrđuje autentičnost poziva niti znači da je osoba već pozvana na ređenje. Izraz „po Duhu“ može opisivati osobni doživljaj, no poziv na zaređenu službu zahtijeva crkveno razlučivanje.
concerns: Ne bi bilo ispravno zaključiti da su dojmljiv govor, osobni osjećaj nadahnuća ili neformalna izjava župnika dovoljni za potvrdu poziva ili za ređenje.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva đakonat razumije kao poseban poziv Duha Svetoga, ali njegovo se razlučivanje odvija i u zajedništvu s Crkvom: kandidat se provjerava, prati i priprema, a crkvena prosudba ima važnu ulogu u potvrđivanju poziva. Ako je kandidat oženjen, u razlučivanje treba uključiti suprugu i obitelj, a potrebni su i prikladna formacija te prikladnost za službu (1 Tim 3,10;). Đakonova je služba trajno služenje po uzoru na Krista slugu, a naviještanje Božje riječi treba biti povezano s njezinim proučavanjem, molitvom i življenjem ().

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding that a diaconal calling can be recognized through service to the community and the encouragement of the parish priest, but the narrative itself does not confirm the authenticity of the calling nor does it mean that the person is already called to ordination. The expression „by the Spirit“ may describe a personal experience, but a calling to ordained ministry requires ecclesial discernment.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church understands the diaconate as a special calling of the Holy Spirit, but its discernment also takes place in communion with the Church: the candidate is tested, accompanied, and prepared, and ecclesial judgment plays an important role in confirming the calling. If the candidate is married, the wife and family should be included in the discernment, and suitable formation and suitability for ministry are also required (1 Tim 3:10;). The deacon's ministry is permanent service modeled after Christ the Servant, and the proclamation of the Word of God should be linked to its study, prayer, and living ().
concerns_en: It would not be correct to conclude that an impressive speech, a personal sense of inspiration, or an informal statement by a parish priest are sufficient to confirm a calling or for ordination.

sections.subtitle_en: Speech at First Communion and an unexpected calling: „We are ordaining you as a deacon“
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts the reaction of the parish priest and the curate after the speech at his son's First Communion
sections.content_en:
The host notes that Krznarić has hardly been in the public eye for the past four years and asks where he has been. The answer is: **he received a calling to the permanent diaconate.**

He did not even know that the permanent diaconate existed, nor had he ever been interested in it. When his son was having his First Communion, the parish priest looked for one of the parents to give a speech. No one volunteered, so the parish priest said: „Come on, you will do it, Zlatko.“ He spoke „by the Spirit“, and as soon as he finished, the curate and the parish priest approached him: *„We are ordaining you as a deacon!“*

He laughed and told them to ordain someone else. But in prayer, that thought kept returning to him. He did not know that a married man could serve close to the altar, so he began to make inquiries.

In the conversation, he states that one of the most famous deacons is **Saint Francis**, who out of humility did not dare to become a priest. For a married candidate, these conditions exist:

- he must be older than 35 years,
- his wife must give her consent,
- he must complete **five years of theological studies**.

The first two conditions were not a problem, but the third one frightened him: *„What college? I was never one for school!“*

sections.subtitle: 580 kilometara na biciklu, s protezom, do Međugorja
sections.screenshot_description: Gost se smije prepričavajući traktor koji ga je štitio od vjetra
sections.content:
Kako bi razlučio poziv, Krznarić je odlučio „ući u ring“ s Bogom. Biciklom je krenuo iz **Čakovca u Međugorje**, oko 580 kilometara. Planirao je usput izmoliti tisuću Zdravo Marija i „podvući crtu“. Nije isplanirao ni rutu ni noćenja, bio je bez kondicije i pripreme, s jednom zdravom nogom i jednom protezom, i potpuno se predao providnosti. Na putu se dogodilo nekoliko zgoda koje naziva „Božjim anegdotama“:

- **Traktor u zavjetrini.** Na putu prema Karlovcu skrenuo je do svetišta blaženog Alojzija Stepinca u Krašiću, gdje nikad nije bio. Pukla mu je guma, a krpanje malom pumpom dugo je trajalo. Zamolio je Boga da mu pošalje traktor koji bi mu bio zavjetrina. Na Dan domovinske zahvalnosti, neradni dan, pred njim se pojavio traktor s prikolicom. Vozio se za njim desetak kilometara i supruzi poslao fotografiju.
- **Soba s Gospinom slikom.** U Slunju je sve bilo zauzeto i skupo. Zavapio je: „Marijo, pa ja k tebi idem, kaj sad tu spavam u nekom kanalu?“ Prišla mu je jedna ženica i ponudila smještaj, malu i jeftinu sobu s velikom Gospinom slikom na sredini.
- **Pumpa kod Plitvica.** Kad mu je kod Plitvičkih jezera ponovno pukla guma, poželio je veliku pumpu. Policajac ga je uputio na samoposlužni servis za bicikle odmah preko puta.
- **Biciklist s krunicom.** Ostao je bez rezervne gume u kraju bez trgovina. Na cesti je zatekao biciklista koji ga je ranije prestigao, a sada se odmarao. Kad mu je Krznarić rekao da ide u Međugorje, čovjek mu je pokazao krunicu i poklonio zračnicu točno potrebne dimenzije.

magisterium.assessment: Opis je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkom vjerom: hodočašće, molitva krunice i traženje Božje volje mogu biti legitimni dijelovi duhovnog razlučivanja, a hodočašće ima biblijske i crkvene korijene. Ipak, razlučivanje se ne bi smjelo svesti na osobni „test” ili zamjenu za razborito promišljanje; iz ovog odlomka nije jasno je li putovanje tako shvaćeno.
concerns: Izraz „ući u ring s Bogom” i plan da nakon tisuću Zdravomarija „podvuče crtu” mogli bi zvučati kao da se od Boga traži određeni znak ili zaključak prema unaprijed zadanom broju molitava; odlomak ne potvrđuje da je to bila njegova namjera.

Putovanje bez isplanirane rute, noćenja, kondicije ili pripreme može upućivati na manjak razboritosti, osobito uz navedenu tjelesnu okolnost. Pouzdanje u providnost ne znači da treba zanemariti odgovornu pripremu i sigurnost.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva hodočašće razumije kao put vjere, a ne samo fizički napor: ono može izražavati traženje Boga i poticati unutarnje obraćenje. Razlučivanje poziva traži molitvu i povjerenje, ali također prudenciju i otvorenost daljnjem ispitivanju; zato iskustvo na putu može biti važno, no samo po sebi ne mora biti konačan dokaz poziva.

Nevertheless, discernment should not be reduced to a personal "test" or a substitute for prudent reflection; from this passage, it is not clear whether the journey was understood in that way.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church understands pilgrimage as a journey of faith, and not merely physical exertion: it can express the search for God and foster interior conversion. Discernment of a calling requires prayer and trust, but also prudence and openness to further examination; therefore, the experience on the road can be important, but in itself does not have to be definitive proof of a calling.
concerns_en: The expression "enter the ring with God" and the plan to "draw a line" after a thousand Hail Marys could sound like asking God for a specific sign or conclusion according to a predetermined number of prayers; the passage does not confirm that this was his intention.

A journey without a planned route, overnight stays, conditioning, or preparation may indicate a lack of prudence, especially given the stated physical circumstance. Trust in providence does not mean that responsible preparation and safety should be neglected.

sections.subtitle_en: 580 kilometers on a bicycle, with a prosthesis, to Međugorje
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest laughs while recounting the tractor that shielded him from the wind
sections.content_en:
In order to discern his calling, Krznarić decided to "enter the ring" with God. He set off by bicycle from **Čakovec to Međugorje**, about 580 kilometers. Along the way, he planned to pray a thousand Hail Marys and "draw a line". He had planned neither a route nor overnight stays, he was without physical conditioning and preparation, with one healthy leg and one prosthesis, and completely surrendered himself to providence. On the way, several events occurred that he calls "God's anecdotes":

- **A tractor in the slipstream.** On the way toward Karlovac, he turned off to the shrine of Blessed Alojzije Stepinac in Krašić, where he had never been. His tire went flat, and patching it with a small pump took a long time. He asked God to send him a tractor that would be a windbreak for him. On Homeland Thanksgiving Day, a non-working day, a tractor with a trailer appeared before him. He rode behind it for about ten kilometers and sent a photo to his wife.
- **A room with Our Lady's picture.** In Slunj, everything was booked and expensive. He cried out: "Mary, I am going to you, why would I sleep here in some ditch now?" A little woman approached him and offered accommodation, a small and inexpensive room with a large picture of Our Lady in the middle.
- **A pump near Plitvice.** When his tire went flat again near Plitvička jezera, he wished for a large pump. A police officer directed him to a self-service bicycle repair station right across the street.
- **A cyclist with a Rosary.** He was left without a spare tire in an area with no shops. On the road, he came across a cyclist who had overtaken him earlier and was now resting. When Krznarić told him he was going to Međugorje, the man showed him a Rosary and gave him an inner tube of the exact required dimensions.

sections.subtitle: „Bože, zar si pozvao mene?“ i odgovor na Podbrdu
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prenosi odgovor koji je u tišini čuo na Podbrdu
sections.content:
U Međugorju je sudjelovao na susretu za obitelji koji organizira **Robert Rukavina**. Žuta dvorana bila je prepuna, prema gostovoj procjeni s 500 do 600 ljudi. Misu je predvodio **fra Petar Ljubičić**. Sandra je znala da se suprug muči s đakonatom i da ga ne želi prihvatiti.

Kod pričesti je fra Petar pitao ima li netko dopuštenje da bude izvanredni djelitelj pričesti. Nitko se nije javio, a zbor je zapjevao: *„Bože, zar si pozvao mene?“* i *„Znam da zoveš, al' se bojim.“* Krznariću su navrle suze, a Sandra mu je šapnula: *„Vidiš, vidiš što propuštaš?“* Odgovorio joj je: „Pusti me.“

Popeo se na **Podbrdo**, do plavog križa, i jadao se Gospi da nije za fakultet i da je toliko zaboravljiv da ne zna zašto je otišao u garažu. Kad je utihnuo i zamolio je da mu odgovori, u tišini je čuo: *„Čekat ću te dok ne prihvatiš poziv.“* Njegova reakcija bila je kratka: *„Joj, užas.“*

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je pretežno pripovjedan i ne iznosi tvrdnju koja bi proturječila katoličkom nauku: spominjanje službe izvanrednog djelitelja pričesti i osobne borbe oko trajnog đakonata uklapa se u različite oblike služenja u Crkvi. Ipak, iz isječka se ne može zaključiti da pjesma ili snažan doživljaj sami po sebi potvrđuju đakonski poziv, koji se razlučuje i živi u crkvenom zajedništvu.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko shvaćanje đakonata naglašava da je riječ o sakramentalno ustanovljenoj službi liturgije, Riječi i ljubavi, a ne samo o osobnoj sklonosti ili osjećaju pozvanosti. Crkva prepoznaje i usmjerava darove vjernika za dobro zajednice; zato osobno iskustvo može biti važan poticaj, ali ga treba razlikovati od crkvenog razlučivanja i primanja sakramenta reda.

However, it cannot be concluded from the excerpt that a song or a powerful experience in itself confirms a diaconal vocation, which is discerned and lived in ecclesial communion.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of the diaconate emphasizes that it is a sacramentally instituted ministry of liturgy, Word, and charity, and not merely a personal inclination or feeling of being called. The Church recognizes and directs the gifts of the faithful for the good of the community; therefore, personal experience can be an important incentive, but it must be distinguished from ecclesial discernment and the reception of the sacrament of Holy Orders.

sections.subtitle_en: “God, did you call me?” and the answer on Podbrdo
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest conveys the answer he heard in silence on Podbrdo
sections.content_en:
In Međugorje, he participated in a meeting for families organized by **Robert Rukavina**. The Yellow Hall was packed, according to the guest's estimate with 500 to 600 people. Mass was led by **fra Petar Ljubičić**. Sandra knew that her husband was struggling with the diaconate and that he did not want to accept it.

At Communion, fra Petar asked if anyone had permission to be an extraordinary minister of Holy Communion. No one answered, and the choir began to sing: *“God, did you call me?”* and *“I know you are calling, but I am afraid.”* Tears welled up in Krznarić's eyes, and Sandra whispered to him: *“Do you see, do you see what you are missing?”* He answered her: “Leave me alone.”

He climbed up to **Podbrdo**, to the Blue Cross, and lamented to Our Lady that he was not cut out for university and that he was so forgetful that he did not know why he went into the garage. When he fell silent and asked her to answer him, he heard in the silence: *“I will wait for you until you accept the call.”* His reaction was short: *“Oh, terrible.”*

sections.subtitle: Klanjanje, monfortanac i biskup kao „drugo mišljenje“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava kako je od biskupa očekivao da će ga osloboditi poziva
sections.content:
Poticaji su se nastavili. Krznarić u župi četvrtkom vodi meditaciju na klanjanju dok prijatelj **Aleks** svira gitaru. Jednom je okupljene pozvao da se predaju Bogu „svim srcem, svom snagom, svom dušom, bez kalkulacije“. U istom trenutku čuo je unutarnji glas: *„Čekam te da mi se predaš, kao što govoriš drugima.“* Rasplakao se, a Aleksu, koji ga je pitao što mu je, odgovorio je samo neka svira.

Zatim je zamolio za molitvu monfortanca **vlč. Zrinka**, kojeg opisuje kao svećenika s darom spoznanja. Ništa mu nije otkrio osim da ima „muku s Gospodinom“. Svećenik je u molitvi rekao: *„Imaš poziv. Gospodin te zove, pogledaj u njega, budi hrabar, kreni, ne boj se.“* Krznarić priznaje da je priželjkivao da mu netko kaže „ne trebaš“, a događalo se upravo suprotno.

Kad je shvatio da „bježi od samoga sebe“, otišao je varaždinskom biskupu **Boži Radošu**. Nadao se da će ga crkveni autoritet osloboditi. Voditelj to duhovito naziva „mišljenjem drugog doktora“. Biskup je, međutim, odgovorio: *„Pa super, bilo bi lijepo da krenete.“* *„Gotovo je, sad stvarno moram“*, zaključio je tada Krznarić.

magisterium.assessment: Klanjanje, poziv na predanje Bogu i traženje svećenikove molitve u skladu su s katoličkom duhovnošću; opisani unutarnji glas može se razumjeti kao osobni poticaj, ali odlomak ne dokazuje da je riječ o izravnoj Božjoj objavi. Takav doživljaj treba razlučivati u molitvi i unutar crkvenog zajedništva, a ne smatrati ga sam po sebi konačnom potvrdom Božje volje.
concerns: Formulacija da je čuo unutarnji glas može, ako se uzme kao sigurna Božja poruka bez daljnjeg razlučivanja, stvoriti dojam da je osjećaj ili snažno iskustvo dostatno za potvrdu njegova značenja.
Odlomak je prekinut nakon riječi „dar”, pa se ne može procijeniti što se točno tvrdi o svećenikovu daru niti kako se taj dar povezuje s molitvom.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razlučivanje priznaje da Bog može poticati čovjeka na različite načine, ali traži molitvu, vrijeme i provjeru nadahnuća u svjetlu vjere i učenja Crkve. Papa Franjo naglašava potrebu za „tišinom dugotrajne molitve” kako bismo mogli ispravno protumačiti poticaje koje vjerujemo da smo primili; zato su suze ili snažna emocija moguće prateće iskustvo, ali nisu sami po sebi dokaz da je poruka od Boga.
