magisterium.assessment_en: Adoration, the call to surrender to God, and seeking a priest's prayer are in accordance with Catholic spirituality; the described inner voice can be understood as a personal prompting, but the passage does not prove that it is a direct revelation from God. Such an experience should be discerned in prayer and within ecclesial communion, rather than being considered in itself a definitive confirmation of God's will.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic discernment recognizes that God can prompt a person in various ways, but it requires prayer, time, and verification of inspirations in the light of faith and the teaching of the Church. Pope Francis emphasizes the need for "the silence of prolonged prayer" so that we may properly interpret the promptings we believe we have received; therefore, tears or strong emotion are a possible accompanying experience, but are not in themselves proof that the message is from God.
concerns_en: The phrasing that he heard an inner voice can, if taken as a certain message from God without further discernment, create the impression that a feeling or strong experience is sufficient to confirm its meaning.
The passage is cut off after the word "gift," so it cannot be evaluated what exactly is claimed about the priest's gift or how that gift relates to prayer.

sections.subtitle_en: Adoration, a Montfortian, and the Bishop as a "Second Opinion"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains how he expected the bishop to relieve him of the calling
sections.content_en:
The promptings continued. On Thursdays in the parish, Krznarić leads meditation at Eucharistic adoration while his friend **Aleks** plays guitar. Once, he invited those gathered to surrender to God "with all their heart, with all their strength, with all their soul, without calculation." At that very moment, he heard an inner voice: *"I am waiting for you to surrender to me, just as you tell others."* He burst into tears, and to Aleks, who asked what was wrong, he only replied that he should keep playing.

Then he asked for prayer from the Montfortian **Fr. Zrinko**, whom he describes as a priest with the gift of knowledge. He revealed nothing to him except that he had a "struggle with the Lord." In prayer, the priest said: *"You have a calling. The Lord is calling you, look to him, be brave, get going, do not be afraid."* Krznarić admits that he wished someone would tell him "you don't have to," but the exact opposite kept happening.

When he realized that he was "running away from himself," he went to the Bishop of Varaždin, **Bože Radoš**. He hoped that the church authority would release him. The host humorously calls this the "second doctor's opinion." The bishop, however, replied: *"Well great, it would be nice for you to start."* *"It's over, now I really have to,"* Krznarić concluded then.

sections.subtitle: „Prestar sam za faks“ i kapelica pokraj Jordanovca
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o kapelici trajnog klanjanja pokraj fakulteta na Jordanovcu
sections.content:
Ostao mu je još jedan izgovor: godine. *„Tko je vidio s 50 godina ići na faks?“* govorio je Bogu. Nekoliko dana kasnije jedna mu je gospođa rekla da su to „prave godine“, jer je njezin otac teologiju upisao s 55 i završio je sa 60 i nešto. Krznarić je pomislio da je taj „još luđi“. Na svaki njegov pokušaj bijega, kaže, Bog mu je na put stavljao ljude koji su mu poručivali: „Ja sam to odlučio, ja te vodim.“

Upisao se na isusovački fakultet na **Jordanovcu**. Ondje mu je najdraže to što se pokraj fakulteta nalazi **kapelica trajnog klanjanja**. Klanjanje silno voli. U njegovoj župi u **Nedelišću** jednom mjesečno održava se cjelodnevno klanjanje i on tada ostaje od početka do kraja, a ako je radni dan, uzima godišnji odmor. *„Ne možemo bolje iskoristiti vrijeme nego biti u Božjoj prisutnosti“*, kaže. Na fakultetu uvijek „prvo dođe Isusu, on je glavni“, a tek onda „ovim zemaljskima“, profesorima.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: dob sama po sebi ne isključuje Božji poziv, a ohrabrenje drugih može pomoći osobi da ozbiljno razmotri svoje mogućnosti. Izraz „ja sam to odlučio, ja te vodim” može se razumjeti kao osobno svjedočanstvo o Božjoj providnosti, ali ne bi ga trebalo tumačiti kao tvrdnju da Bog ukida ljudsku slobodu ili da je svaka okolnost nepogrešiv znak poziva.
concerns: Ako se rečenica o Božjoj odluci shvati kao neizbježna sudbina koja čovjeku ne ostavlja prostor za slobodan odgovor i razlučivanje, to bi bilo u napetosti s katoličkim razumijevanjem poziva kao dijaloga s Bogom.
magisterium.enrichment: Sveto pismo prikazuje kako Bog povjerava važne zadaće i ljudima u starijoj dobi: Mojsije je bio star kada mu je povjerena misija vođenja Izraela, a Abrahamov poziv također pokazuje da Božje djelovanje nije ograničeno ljudskim očekivanjima o životnoj dobi. Katoličko razumijevanje poziva ipak uključuje i Božju inicijativu i slobodan ljudski odgovor; stoga poticaje drugih valja primiti kao moguću pomoć u razlučivanju, a ne automatski kao konačan dokaz Božje volje.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: age in itself does not exclude God's call, and encouragement from others can help a person seriously consider their options. The expression "I have decided this, I am leading you" can be understood as a personal testimony of God's providence, but it should not be interpreted as a claim that God abolishes human freedom or that every circumstance is an infallible sign of a vocation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Sacred Scripture shows that God entrusts important tasks also to people of advanced age: Moses was old when he was entrusted with the mission of leading Israel, and Abraham's call also shows that God's action is not limited by human expectations regarding age. The Catholic understanding of vocation nevertheless includes both God's initiative and a free human response; therefore, the encouragements of others should be received as possible help in discernment, and not automatically as definitive proof of God's will.
concerns_en: If the sentence about God's decision is understood as an inevitable fate that leaves no room for man's free response and discernment, that would be in tension with the Catholic understanding of vocation as a dialogue with God.

sections.subtitle_en: "I'm too old for college" and the chapel next to Jordanovac
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the chapel of perpetual Eucharistic adoration next to the faculty on Jordanovac
sections.content_en:
He had one more excuse left: age. *"Who ever heard of going to college at 50?"* he would say to God. A few days later, a lady told him that those were the "right years," because her father enrolled in theology at 55 and finished it at 60-something. Krznarić thought that that man was "even crazier." To his every attempt to escape, he says, God placed people in his path who conveyed to him: "I have decided this, I am leading you."

He enrolled in the Jesuit faculty on **Jordanovac**. What he likes most there is that next to the faculty there is a **chapel of perpetual Eucharistic adoration**. He loves Eucharistic adoration immensely. In his parish in **Nedelišće**, an all-day Eucharistic adoration is held once a month and he then stays from beginning to end, and if it is a workday, he takes annual leave. *"We cannot use time better than to be in God's presence,"* he says. At the faculty, he always "first comes to Jesus, He is the main one," and only then to "these earthly ones," the professors.

sections.subtitle: Ispiti pred Presvetim: petica, pet pitanja i test koji nije podijeljen
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava kako se profesor predomislio i umjesto pismenog ispita ga ispitao usmeno
sections.content:
Krznarić je sada na četvrtoj godini. Položio je hebrejski, latinski, grčki i „sve te filozofije“. Naglašava da ne govori „racionalno“, nego iz odnosa s Bogom, i iznosi niz zgoda s ispita:

- **Psihologija kod patera Mije Nikića.** Pred Presvetim je rekao: „Ako je to od tebe poziv, dobit ću peticu, i to mi je znak da si ti sa mnom.“ Profesor ga je pitao upravo ono što je najbolje znao i na kraju rekao: „Kad bi bar redoviti studenti ovako dobro učili!“
- **Srednjovjekovna filozofija.** Literatura su bile dvije knjige po 500 stranica sitnog tiska, koje mu je Sandra donijela iz knjižnice, i skripta od stotinjak stranica. Večer prije ispita htio je ponavljati, ali je u molitvi osjetio poziv: „Idi na svetu misu u znak zahvale za ispit koji bi sutra prošao.“ Otišao je. Sutradan mu je pred učionicom nepoznati student nabrojio pet pitanja koja profesor obično postavlja. Upravo su ta pitanja došla na ispitu, a tog studenta nikad više nije vidio.
- **Sociologija kod profesora Peračkovića.** Bojao se pismenog dijela s 30 do 40 pitanja nakon kojeg slijedi usmeni. Pred Presvetim je molio da ga profesor ispita samo usmeno. Profesor je na ispitu podigao test, gledao ga, spustio ga i rekao: „Predomislio sam se, pitat ću vas usmeno.“ Dobio je desetku. Sutradan mu je profesor napisao e-mail da je ponio test, „ali ga nije mogao dati“. Krznarić mu je odgovorio da je upravo za to molio, a na kraju su razmijenili knjige.
- **Moralna teologija.** Prije dva tjedna izašao je na ispit nedovoljno pripremljen, jer je dan ranije svjedočio u jednoj župi, a skriptu sa sitnim slovima slabo je vidio. Zadihan je stigao biciklom, nakon što ga je izvadio iz kamiona, i ušao s pet odlikaša. Ispit je trajao oko sat vremena. Dobio je osmicu, a profesor mu je rekao: „Vi ste najviše govorili po duhu.“ Kolege su to primijetile, a on je to doživio kao potvrdu.

Uz to se nasmijao i opisu svoje rutine: navečer kamionom vozi do Zagreba, ponavlja gradivo u tišini, a onda „kao pravi student“ biciklom odlazi na fakultet.

magisterium.assessment: Molitva pred Presvetim i traženje Božjeg vodstva mogu biti dio razboritog razlučivanja poziva, pa sama zgoda nije protivna katoličkom nauku. Ipak, postavljanje ocjene kao znaka koji bi potvrdio poziv može biti teološki nejasno ako se uspjeh na ispitu uzima kao siguran dokaz Božje volje.
concerns: Moguće je iskušavati Boga ako se od njega zahtijeva određeni znak kao jamstvo poziva, umjesto da se znak moli ponizno i uvjetno.
Ispitna ocjena sama po sebi ne potvrđuje crkveni poziv; mogla bi se pogrešno protumačiti kao nedvojben odgovor Boga.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razlučivanje može uključivati molitvu i znakove, ali traženje znaka radi spoznaje onoga što je Bogu milo ne mora samo po sebi biti iskušavanje Boga; važni su svrha i način traženja. Poziv se ipak razlučuje razborito, uz oslonac na nauk vjere, a ne prvenstveno na unutarnji dojam ili jedan povoljan događaj. Zrelost poziva uključuje otvorenost daljnjem razlučivanju i poniznu nadu, a ne tvrdnju da je Božja volja već potpuno i nepogrešivo utvrđena.

magisterium.assessment_en: Prayer before the Blessed Sacrament and seeking God's guidance can be part of a prudent discernment of a vocation, so the incident itself is not contrary to Catholic teaching. Nevertheless, setting a grade as a sign that would confirm a vocation can be theologically ambiguous if exam success is taken as certain proof of God's will.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic discernment can include prayer and signs, but seeking a sign in order to know what is pleasing to God does not in itself have to be tempting God; the purpose and the manner of seeking are important. A vocation is nevertheless discerned prudently, relying on the teaching of the faith, and not primarily on an internal impression or a single favorable event. Maturity of a vocation includes openness to further discernment and humble hope, rather than claiming that God's will is already completely and infallibly established.
concerns_en: It is possible to tempt God if a specific sign is demanded of Him as a guarantee of a vocation, instead of praying for a sign humbly and conditionally.
An exam grade in itself does not confirm an ecclesial vocation; it could be misinterpreted as an unequivocal answer from God.

sections.subtitle_en: Exams before the Blessed Sacrament: a five, five questions, and a test that was not handed out
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts how the professor changed his mind and examined him orally instead of giving a written exam
sections.content_en:
Krznarić is now in his fourth year. He passed Hebrew, Latin, Greek, and "all those philosophies." He emphasizes that he does not speak "rationally," but out of a relationship with God, and presents a series of incidents from exams:

- **Psychology with Father Mijo Nikić.** Before the Blessed Sacrament, he said: "If this call is from you, I will get a five, and that is a sign to me that you are with me." The professor asked him precisely what he knew best and said in the end: "If only regular students studied this well!"
- **Medieval Philosophy.** The required reading consisted of two 500-page books in fine print, which Sandra had brought him from the library, and a study guide of about a hundred pages. The evening before the exam, he wanted to review, but in prayer he felt a calling: "Go to Holy Mass in thanksgiving for the exam that you would pass tomorrow." He went. The next day, in front of the classroom, an unknown student listed five questions that the professor usually asks. Those very questions appeared on the exam, and he never saw that student again.
- **Sociology with Professor Peračković.** He was afraid of the written part with 30 to 40 questions, followed by the oral exam. Before the Blessed Sacrament, he prayed that the professor would examine him only orally. At the exam, the professor picked up the test, looked at it, put it down, and said: "I changed my mind, I will examine you orally." He received a ten. The next day, the professor wrote him an email saying he had brought the test, "but he could not hand it out." Krznarić replied to him that he had prayed for that very thing, and in the end they exchanged books.
- **Moral Theology.** Two weeks ago, he took an exam insufficiently prepared, because the day before he had given a testimony in a parish, and he could barely read the small print of the study guide. He arrived out of breath on a bicycle, after taking it out of his truck, and entered with five top students. The exam lasted about an hour. He received an eight, and the professor said to him: "You spoke most according to the spirit." His colleagues noticed this, and he experienced it as a confirmation.

In addition, he laughed at the description of his routine: in the evening he drives a truck to Zagreb, reviews the material in silence, and then "like a real student" rides a bicycle to the faculty.

sections.subtitle: Zašto je nestao iz javnosti i dug put do ređenja
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava žrtvu studiranja uz posao i obitelj
sections.content:
*„Bog je vjeran, i to je ono najbitnije“*, sažima Krznarić. Na fakultet se, kaže, „bacio na glavu“, iako nije mlad ni „posložen“. Ne zna hoće li završiti, ali živi dan po dan: *„Nemam ni jučer, nemam ni sutra, imam danas. I to ti, Bože, hoću dati.“*

To je ujedno i odgovor na voditeljevo pitanje gdje je bio posljednje četiri godine. Studij je toliko zahtjevan da bi se, kaže, trebao baviti samo njime, a on cijeli dan radi, kod kuće ga čeka „masa stvari“, a tu je i društveni život. Mnogo je toga morao „odrezati“.

Nada se da će uz Božju pomoć završiti preostalu godinu studija. Nakon pet godina fakulteta slijede **još tri godine puta prema đakonatu**.

Dodaje i zanimljivost. Kad je krenuo, prijatelj ga je upozorio da đakoni dugo nisu ređeni, možda deset ili više godina, te da se ne može postati đakonom s tjelesnim nedostatkom, „ako ti fali i prst“. Krznarić je odgovorio da vjeruje Gospodinu. Kasnije je doznao da su kanonski propisi promijenjeni, pa i netko s protezom, poput njega, može biti zaređen. Ređenja su ponovno započela i sada je u tijeku jedan ciklus.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na Božjoj vjernosti, povjerenju i predanju svakodnevice Bogu u skladu je s kršćanskom vjerom; Benedikt XVI. također podsjeća da se kršćanski život oslanja na Božju vjernost i povjerenje u njega. Odlomak ne prikazuje zahtjevnost studija kao razlog za odustajanje od poziva, nego kao stvarnu teškoću, pa u navedenom tekstu nema bitnog odstupanja od katoličkog nauka.
magisterium.enrichment: Izraz da ima samo danas može se razumjeti kao predanje sadašnjega dana Bogu, a ne kao poricanje odgovornosti za prošlost ili buduće obveze. Biblijski poticaj da se bude spreman obrazložiti nadu u sebi podupire ozbiljnost teološkog studija, a Benedikt XVI. izričito ističe njegovu važnost u formaciji za služenje Crkvi.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on God's faithfulness, trust, and surrendering everyday life to God is in accordance with the Christian faith; Benedict XVI also recalls that Christian life relies on God's faithfulness and trust in Him. The passage does not present the demanding nature of study as a reason to give up on a vocation, but as a real difficulty, so in the cited text there is no substantial departure from Catholic teaching.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The expression of having only today can be understood as surrendering the present day to God, rather than as a denial of responsibility for the past or future obligations. The biblical exhortation to be ready to give an explanation for the hope within supports the seriousness of theological study, and Benedict XVI explicitly emphasizes its importance in formation for service to the Church.

sections.subtitle_en: Why he disappeared from the public eye and the long road to ordination
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the sacrifice of studying alongside work and family
sections.content_en:
*"God is faithful, and that is what matters most,"* Krznarić summarizes. He says he "dove headfirst" into college, even though he is neither young nor "all set." He does not know if he will finish, but he lives day by day: *"I have neither yesterday nor tomorrow, I have today. And that, God, I want to give to You."*

That is also the answer to the host's question about where he has been for the past four years. The studies are so demanding that, he says, he should be doing only that, yet he works all day, "a mass of things" awaits him at home, and then there is social life. He had to "cut off" a lot of things.

He hopes that with God's help he will finish the remaining year of study. After five years of faculty, **another three years of the journey toward the diaconate** follow.

He also adds an interesting detail. When he started, a friend warned him that deacons had not been ordained for a long time, perhaps ten or more years, and that one cannot become a deacon with a physical defect, "even if you're missing a finger." Krznarić replied that he trusts the Lord. Later he learned that canonical regulations had been changed, so even someone with a prosthesis, like him, can be ordained. Ordinations have started again and now one cycle is underway.

sections.subtitle: Što đakon smije, a što ne: od krštenja do supstancijalne promjene
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava supstancijalnu promjenu na primjeru papira koji izgara u pepeo
sections.content:
Krznarić objašnjava ovlasti đakona nakon završene formacije. Đakon može gotovo sve, osim **pretvorbe na svetoj misi i ispovijedi**, a time ni bolesničkog pomazanja, uz koje obično ide ispovijed. Đakon može:

- krstiti,
- vjenčavati,
- voditi sprovode,
- dijeliti pričest,
- čitati evanđelje,
- pomagati u svemu što župnik odredi.

Kako bi približio pojam pretvorbe, gost se „teološki izražava“. Supstancijalna promjena, kaže, nastaje kad se materija „u jezgri“ pretvori u nešto drugo, primjerice kad zapaljeni papir postane pepeo. Nešto se slično, prema njegovu objašnjenju, događa kad hostija postaje Tijelo Kristovo, a to može samo svećenik.

Voditelj dodaje širi kontekst. Crkva je suočena s **krizom poziva**, a Hrvatska, iako još stoji bolje od drugih zemalja, ne bi se smjela opustiti. Trajni đakonat vidi kao način da se pozivi ojačaju i da Crkva bude prisutnija. Gostu poručuje da je „na pola puta“ i da vjeruje kako će ga „izgurati do kraja“.

magisterium.assessment: Opis glavnih službi đakona uglavnom je usklađen s katoličkim naukom: đakon može krstiti, naviještati evanđelje, dijeliti pričest, sudjelovati u sklapanju ženidbe i voditi sprovodne obrede, ali ne predsjeda euharistijskoj pretvorbi. Ipak, izraz „može gotovo sve” i tvrdnja da smije činiti sve što mu župnik odredi preširoki su, a usporedba pretvorbe s papirom koji postaje pepeo može zamagliti nauk o euharistijskoj prisutnosti.
concerns: „Može gotovo sve” može pogrešno sugerirati da đakon ima ovlasti svećenika; đakon je zaređen za služenje u liturgiji, naviještanju Riječi i ljubavi, ali ne može predsjedati euharistijskoj pretvorbi.
Ovlasti đakona nisu određene samo onime što župnik odredi: ovise o crkvenom pravu i potrebnim ovlaštenjima. Primjerice, ženidbu đakon može asistirati i blagosloviti uz propisano ovlaštenje.

Usporedba s papirom koji izgori u pepeo nije dostatno objašnjenje pretvorbe. U euharistiji se, prema katoličkom nauku, mijenja sama bit kruha i vina, dok njihova osjetilna svojstva ostaju; izvadak ne prikazuje ostatak objašnjenja, pa se ne može procijeniti je li gost tu razliku kasnije pojasnio.
magisterium.enrichment: Đakon je primio sakrament svetoga reda, ali u stupnju služenja: njegovo poslanje uključuje liturgiju, naviještanje Riječi i ljubav, a ne svećeničko predsjedanje euharistijom i njezino posvećenje. Krštenje, razdioba pričesti i određene službe u ženidbi i sprovodu stvarne su đakonske službe, ali izvršavaju se unutar crkvenog poretka i uz potrebna ovlaštenja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the main ministries of a deacon is mostly aligned with Catholic teaching: a deacon can baptize, proclaim the Gospel, distribute Communion, assist at the celebration of marriage, and lead funeral rites, but does not preside over the Eucharistic consecration. However, the expression "can do almost everything" and the claim that he may do everything the parish priest determines are too broad, and the comparison of the consecration to paper becoming ash can obscure the teaching on the Eucharistic presence.
magisterium.enrichment_en: A deacon has received the sacrament of Holy Orders, but in the degree of service: his mission includes liturgy, the proclamation of the Word, and charity, not the priestly presiding over the Eucharist and its consecration. Baptism, the distribution of Communion, and certain ministries in marriage and funerals are actual diaconal ministries, but they are carried out within the ecclesial order and with the necessary faculties.
concerns_en: "Can do almost everything" can mistakenly suggest that a deacon has the faculties of a priest; a deacon is ordained for service in liturgy, the proclamation of the Word, and charity, but cannot preside over the Eucharistic consecration.

The faculties of a deacon are not determined solely by what the parish priest determines: they depend on canon law and the necessary faculties. For example, a deacon may assist at and bless a marriage with the prescribed faculty.

The comparison to paper burning into ash is not an adequate explanation of the consecration. In the Eucharist, according to Catholic teaching, the very substance of the bread and wine changes, while their sensible properties remain; the excerpt does not show the rest of the explanation, so it cannot be evaluated whether the guest clarified this distinction later.

sections.subtitle_en: What a deacon may and may not do: from baptism to substantial change
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains substantial change using the example of paper burning into ash
sections.content_en:
Krznarić explains the faculties of a deacon after completing formation. A deacon can do almost everything, except **consecration at Holy Mass and confession**, and thereby neither the anointing of the sick, which usually goes with confession. A deacon can:

- baptize,
- officiate marriages,
- lead funerals,
- distribute Communion,
- read the Gospel,
- help with everything the parish priest determines.

In order to explain the concept of consecration, the guest "expresses himself theologically." Substantial change, he says, occurs when matter "at its core" turns into something else, for example when burning paper becomes ash. Something similar, according to his explanation, happens when the host becomes the Body of Christ, and only a priest can do that.

The host adds broader context. The Church is faced with a **crisis of vocations**, and Croatia, although still doing better than other countries, should not relax. He sees the permanent diaconate as a way to strengthen vocations and make the Church more present. He tells the guest that he is "halfway there" and that he believes he will "push it through to the end."

sections.subtitle: „Ne ‚Bože, daj‘, nego ‚Bože, evo me‘“: poruka onima koji osjećaju poziv
sections.screenshot_description: Gost poziva na molitvu „Bože, evo me, tu sam“
sections.content:
Na kraju razgovora voditelj traži riječi ohrabrenja za one koji razmišljaju o trajnom đakonatu. Krznarić spominje prijatelja s **desetero djece** koji je također dobio poziv. Taj prijatelj dobro poznaje iste strahove: hoće li to moći, sramotu iz djetinjstva kad te profesor prozove pred ploču i pitanje kako se sramotiti s pedeset godina. Unatoč tome, redovito studira i „sve rješava“.

Bog, kaže gost, ne gleda jesi li mehaničar, vozač ili imaš dva fakulteta, nego srce, vjernost i odanost. Govori i o žrtvi:

> *„Kad ideš bliže Bogu, ideš bliže križu… Koliko si više spreman na žrtvu, toliko si više upotrebljiv za Boga.“*

Bog nas, prema njegovim riječima, često „izresetira“, uzme staro i „stavi novo odijelo“, pa čovjek zna da više nije svoj, nego Njegov.

Kao primjer navodi svoje subote. S nekolicinom prijatelja odlazi u kapelicu trajnog klanjanja kod franjevaca u **Varaždinu** od šest do sedam ujutro, zatim na misu i na molitvu krunice na koljenima. U nedjelju je opet na klanjanju u šest. Taj „komadić sna“ smatra malom žrtvom za Gospodina, jer „u Gospodinu ili sabireš ili rasipaš“.

Ključno je, zaključuje, odmaknuti se od molitve **„Bože, daj“** prema molitvi **„Bože, evo me, tu sam. Idem kamo ti želiš“**. Bog čeka naš „da“ i računa na nas.

magisterium.assessment: Opis ohrabrenja uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim razumijevanjem poziva: nesigurnost i osjećaj nedostatnosti ne isključuju poziv, a vjernost i raspoloživost važne su za odgovor Bogu. Ipak, tvrdnju da Bog ne gleda zanimanje ni obrazovanje treba razumjeti kao naglasak na dostojanstvu osobe, a ne kao da sposobnosti, formacija i crkveno razlučivanje nisu važni.
concerns: Izjava o tome da Bog gleda srce može, ako se uzme izdvojeno, stvoriti dojam kako dobra volja sama dostaje za đakonsko zaređenje; Crkva predviđa formaciju i provjeru prikladnosti, a kod oženjenog kandidata važni su i informirani pristanak supruge i razgovor s obitelji.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razlučivanje ne traži da kandidat unaprijed bude siguran u vlastitu sposobnost, nego da poziv provjerava u molitvi, uz pratnju Crkve i otvorenost za daljnje razlučivanje; pouzdanje se oslanja na Boga, a ne samo na samoprocjenu vlastitih darova. Đakonat je sakramentalna služba Božjem narodu, pa se poziv oblikuje kroz pripravu i potvrdu Crkve, a ne samo kroz osobni osjećaj pozvanosti. Kod oženjenog kandidata razlučivanje uključuje i suprugu te obitelj, a pristanak supruge mora biti informiran.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of encouragement is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding of vocation: uncertainty and a sense of inadequacy do not exclude a vocation, and fidelity and availability are important for responding to God. However, the claim that God does not look at profession or education should be understood as an emphasis on the dignity of the person, and not as if abilities, formation, and ecclesial discernment were not important.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic discernment does not require a candidate to be certain of his own ability in advance, but rather to test the calling in prayer, with the accompaniment of the Church and openness to further discernment; confidence relies on God, not merely on the self-assessment of one's own gifts. The diaconate is a sacramental ministry to the people of God, so the vocation is shaped through preparation and confirmation by the Church, and not merely through a personal sense of being called. For a married candidate, discernment also includes the wife and family, and the wife's consent must be informed.
concerns_en: The statement that God looks at the heart can, if taken in isolation, create the impression that good will alone is sufficient for diaconal ordination; the Church provides for formation and verification of suitability, and in the case of a married candidate, the informed consent of the wife and discussion with the family are also important.

sections.subtitle_en: "Not 'God, give', but 'God, here I am'": a message to those who feel a calling
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest calls for the prayer "God, here I am, I am here"
sections.content_en:
At the end of the conversation, the host asks for words of encouragement for those considering the permanent diaconate. Krznarić mentions a friend with **ten children** who also received a calling. That friend knows the same fears well: whether he will be able to do it, the shame from childhood when a professor calls you to the blackboard, and the question of how to embarrass yourself at fifty years old. Despite that, he studies regularly and "solves everything".

God, the guest says, does not look at whether you are a mechanic, a driver, or have two degrees, but at the heart, fidelity, and devotion. He also speaks about sacrifice:

> *"When you go closer to God, you go closer to the cross… The more you are ready for sacrifice, the more useful you are to God."*

God, according to his words, often "resets" us, takes the old and "puts on a new suit", so a person knows that he is no longer his own, but His.

As an example, he mentions his Saturdays. With a few friends, he goes to the chapel of perpetual adoration at the Franciscans in **Varaždin** from six to seven in the morning, then to Mass and to praying the Rosary on their knees. On Sunday, he is at adoration again at six. He considers that "little piece of sleep" a small sacrifice for the Lord, because "in the Lord you either gather or scatter".

The key is, he concludes, to move away from the prayer **"God, give"** toward the prayer **"God, here I am, I am here. I go where you want"**. God awaits our "yes" and counts on us.

sections.subtitle: Blic pitanja: tišina umjesto dvorane, poziv umjesto straha od neuspjeha
sections.screenshot_description: Gost odgovara na blic pitanja u formatu „ili-ili“
sections.content:
Voditelj zatim gosta „rešeta kao pravog studenta“ blic pitanjima u formatu „ili-ili“. Krznarić ga u šali moli da ne pita ništa iz teologije.

- **Život prije ili poslije obraćenja?** „Apsolutno poslije obraćenja.“ Voditelj zaključuje: „Dvojka osigurana.“
- **Tišina i molitva ili svjedočenje pred punom dvoranom?** Tišina i molitva. Sve više „bježi od ljudi“, a na podcast je došao samo zato što mu je Gospodin u molitvi rekao da ide. Inače bi, priznaje, odbio poziv.
- **Teži križ ili veće poslanje?** Nakon duge stanke odgovara da bi pitao Gospodina i da je spreman na oboje. Unutarnji glas ne smatra svojim posjedom, nego nezasluženom milošću, i ne dobiva uvijek odgovor.
- **Biti nepoznat ili javno svjedočiti?** „Lakše je biti nepoznat, ali ako treba, svjedočio bih javno. To ima svoju cijenu i spreman sam je platiti.“
- **Strah od neuspjeha ili strah od propuštenog poziva?** Radije bi se odazvao Gospodinu. Neuspjeha se ne boji, jer je on „sastavni dio uspjeha“: tko ne padne, ne može rasti.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na obraćenju, tišini i molitvi u skladu je s katoličkom duhovnošću, a osobni izbor tišine umjesto javnog nastupa sam po sebi nije protiv Evanđelja. Ipak, tvrdnju da mu je Gospodin u molitvi rekao da dođe treba shvatiti kao osobno duhovno iskustvo koje zahtijeva razborito razlučivanje, a ne kao nešto što se može potvrditi samo na temelju odlomka.
concerns: Izraz da sve više „bježi od ljudi” može označavati osobnu sklonost povučenosti, ali ako bi značio trajno izbjegavanje bližnjih ili zanemarivanje poslanja, bio bi u napetosti s kršćanskim pozivom na svjedočenje i služenje.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička duhovnost ne suprotstavlja kontemplaciju svjedočenju: crkveni nauk opisuje kako tiha kontemplacija vodi prema potrebi da se s drugima podijeli ono što je čovjek susreo u Bogu. Obraćenje je trajni odgovor na Božji poziv, a kršćansko svjedočenje uključuje i riječi i život; stoga povlačenje može biti plodno ako osnažuje ljubav i služenje, a ne postaje bijeg od njih.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on conversion, silence, and prayer is in accordance with Catholic spirituality, and the personal choice of silence over public speaking is not in itself against the Gospel. Nevertheless, the claim that the Lord told him in prayer to come should be understood as a personal spiritual experience that requires prudent discernment, and not as something that can be confirmed solely on the basis of the passage.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic spirituality does not oppose contemplation to witnessing: Church teaching describes how quiet contemplation leads toward the need to share with others what one has encountered in God. Conversion is an ongoing response to God's call, and Christian witnessing includes both words and life; therefore, withdrawal can be fruitful if it strengthens love and service, rather than becoming an escape from them.
concerns_en: The expression that he increasingly "flees from people" may indicate a personal inclination toward seclusion, but if it were to mean a permanent avoidance of one's neighbors or a neglect of mission, it would be in tension with the Christian call to witnessing and service.

sections.subtitle_en: Lightning questions: silence instead of a hall, a calling instead of fear of failure
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest answers lightning questions in an "either-or" format
sections.content_en:
The host then "grills the guest like a real student" with lightning questions in an "either-or" format. Krznarić jokingly asks him not to ask anything from theology.

- **Life before or after conversion?** "Absolutely after conversion." The host concludes: "A passing grade secured."
- **Silence and prayer or witnessing before a full hall?** Silence and prayer. He increasingly "flees from people," and he came to the podcast only because the Lord told him in prayer to go. Otherwise, he admits, he would have declined the invitation.
- **A heavier cross or a greater mission?** After a long pause, he answers that he would ask the Lord and that he is ready for both. He does not consider the inner voice his possession, but an unmerited grace, and he does not always receive an answer.
- **Being unknown or witnessing publicly?** "It is easier to be unknown, but if necessary, I would witness publicly. That has its price and I am ready to pay it."
- **Fear of failure or fear of a missed calling?** He would rather respond to the Lord. He is not afraid of failure, because it is an "integral part of success": whoever does not fall cannot grow.

sections.subtitle: Blagoslov na rastanku i najava sljedeće Redefinicije
sections.screenshot_description: Gost na kraju razgovora zaziva Božji blagoslov na obitelji
sections.content:
Voditelj zahvaljuje Krznariću što se odazvao i pozivu i podcastu te zaziva blagoslov na njega, njegovu obitelj, poziv, ispite i studij. Gost uzvraća molitvom: *„Neka dragi Bog blagoslovi, čuva nas, naše obitelji, naše planove, misli, da budemo njegovi. Amen.“*

Voditelj poziva gledatelje da lajkaju, dijele i pretplate se na kanal te da prate profil na **Patreonu**, gdje se sljedeća epizoda može pogledati odmah.

U najavi sljedeće epizode sugovornik iznosi provokativnu misao. Čovječanstvo, kaže, ne zna da Bog postoji jer se katolici, umjesto da se mole na javnim mjestima i napuste svaki položaj koji je u suprotnosti s vjerom, skrivaju kad se mole i pričešćuju se „kad nitko nije u crkvi“.

magisterium.assessment: Zahvala, zazivanje Božjeg blagoslova za gosta i njegovu obitelj te zajednička molitva u skladu su s katoličkom pobožnošću i shvaćanjem obitelji kao mjesta vjere i svjedočenja. Najava sljedeće epizode ostaje nedovršena, pa se njezina teološka tvrdnja ne može pouzdano procijeniti.
concerns: Najava provokativne misli o tome zašto čovječanstvo ne zna da Bog postoji prekinuta je prije iznošenja razloga, pa se njezin sadržaj ne može ocijeniti.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička liturgijska tradicija uključuje molitve kojima se za obitelj zazivaju Božja zaštita, sloga i sposobnost da vjeru svjedoči riječju i primjerom. Takva molitva nije sama po sebi liturgijski čin blagoslova, nego prošnja Bogu; u ovom odlomku ona izražava zahvalnost i povjerenje u Boga. Svjedočenje vjere u obiteljskom i javnom životu povezano je s kršćanskim pozivom naviještanja Evanđelja.

magisterium.assessment_en: Thanksgiving, the invocation of God's blessing for the guest and his family, and communal prayer are in accordance with Catholic piety and the understanding of the family as a place of faith and witness. The preview of the next episode remains incomplete, so its theological assertion cannot be reliably evaluated.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic liturgical tradition includes prayers by which God's protection, harmony, and the ability to witness to the faith by word and example are invoked for the family. Such a prayer is not in itself a liturgical act of blessing, but a petition to God; in this passage, it expresses gratitude and trust in God. Witnessing to the faith in family and public life is connected to the Christian vocation of proclaiming the Gospel.

sections.content_en:
The host thanks Krznarić for responding to both the call and the podcast and invokes a blessing upon him, his family, calling, exams, and studies. The guest responds with a prayer: *„May dear God bless, protect us, our families, our plans, thoughts, so that we may be His. Amen.“*

The host invites viewers to like, share, and subscribe to the channel and to follow the profile on **Patreon**, where the next episode can be watched immediately.

In the preview of the next episode, the interlocutor presents a provocative thought. Humanity, he says, does not know that God exists because Catholics, instead of praying in public places and abandoning every position that is contrary to the faith, hide when they pray and receive Communion „when no one is in the church“.
